# Money Map — raffle.fun (Raffle clone + RaffleFactory)

Built by the orchestrator from `DESIGN.md` (clean spec) plus source. Line numbers are `Raffle.sol` unless prefixed `F:` (`RaffleFactory.sol`) or `I:` (`IRaffle.sol`).
Empty / N/A surfaces: no shares, exchange rate, index, interest, yield, liquidation, oracle price, or cross-chain message. The only accrual is the fixed-price pot, split once by constant BPS. The async VRF request/callback pair is the only two-phase message. Lenses whose primary surface does not exist here should work the closest analogue named below rather than hunt totals that do not exist.

## 1. Assets

| Asset | Enters via | Leaves via |
| --- | --- | --- |
| USDC (`quoteToken`, trusted, 6 dp) | `buyEntries` `safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, this, entryCount*1e6)` :224 | `refundTickets` :369 (to ticket owner), `redeemWinningTicket` CashWon :342 (to winner), `releaseSponsorProceeds` :380 (to `sponsorRecipient`), `releaseProtocolFees` :390 (to `protocolTreasury`). All via `_transferQuote` :564, which screens `_isProtocolDestination` :593. |
| Prize ERC-721 (untrusted contract per DESIGN.md) | `F:createRaffle` `prize.safeTransferFrom(sponsor, raffle, id)` F:128 → `onERC721Received` :416 flips `AwaitingPrize→Active` :428; factory verifies `ownerOf` F:129 and `status()==Active` F:132 | `redeemWinningTicket` NftWon `transferFrom(this, winner, id)` :334 + `ownerOf` check :335; `releaseSponsorPrize` (CashWon or Refunding) :404 + check :405 |
| Native ETH | `requestDraw` `msg.value` :240 (`receive()` reverts :171) | wrapper fee `requestRandomWordsInNative{value: requestPrice}` (consumer base) via :257; excess `call` to `msg.sender` :267 |
| Ticket ERC-721 (this contract) | minted in `buyEntries` `_safeMint` :235 (one ticket per purchase, range `[first,last]`) | burned in `refundTickets` :364 or `redeemWinningTicket` :325; freely transferable in every state, screened by `_update` :497 |

Untracked: USDC sent directly to a clone, ETH forced via selfdestruct, NFTs sent with unsafe `transferFrom` (NatSpec :410). No sweep exists; surplus is stuck by design.

## 2. Tracked totals (every writer)

| Variable | Writes (+ / − / =) |
| --- | --- |
| `unsettledPot` | `+= grossAmount` buyEntries :233 · `= 0` enableRefunds :297 (moved to `remainingRefundLiability`) · `= 0` `_settleWinningTicket` :553 (split into the three claims) |
| `remainingRefundLiability` | `= unsettledPot` enableRefunds :298 · `-= amount` refundTickets :368 |
| `winnerProceeds` | `= cashAmount` `_settleWinningTicket` CashWon branch only :548 · `= 0` redeem CashWon branch :341 |
| `sponsorProceeds` | `= sponsorAmount` `_settleWinningTicket` :554 · `= 0` releaseSponsorProceeds :378 |
| `protocolFees` | `= protocolFee` `_settleWinningTicket` :555 · `= 0` releaseProtocolFees :388 |
| `accountedQuoteBalance()` :468 | view = sum of the five above |
| `totalEntries` (uint128) | `= lastEntry` buyEntries :230 only (lifetime; never decremented by refunds/burns) |
| `ticketCount` (uint128) | `++` buyEntries :231 only |
| `_ticketRanges[id]` | set buyEntries :232; never cleared (historical after burn, :138) |
| flags | `settlementComplete` :551 · `winningTicketId` :552 · `winnerRedeemed` :324 · `winnerRecipient` :323 · `prizeClaimed` :331 / :403 — all set-once, never reset |
| VRF state | `status=Drawing` :252 · `drawRequestedAt` :253 · `_requestInFlight` :254/:260 · `vrfRequestId` :259 · `winningEntry` :519 · `resolvedAt` :520 · `status=NftWon/CashWon` :521 |
| `status` | ctor `Refunding` :165 (implementation lock) · init `AwaitingPrize` :205 · `Active` :428 · `Drawing` :252 · `NftWon/CashWon` :521 · `Refunding` :299 |
| Factory | `raffleCount` F:105 · `raffleById` F:123 · `idByRaffle` F:124 · `isRaffle` F:125 (set BEFORE the prize transfer F:128) |

Split math (`_settleWinningTicket` :539-555): `fee = mulDiv(pot,500,1e4)`; NftWon `sponsor = pot - fee`; CashWon `cash = mulDiv(pot,8000,1e4)`, `sponsor = pot - fee - cash`. Because `pot` is always a multiple of 1e6, all three are exact (no dust) — verify, do not assume.

## 3. Asymmetry table

| Total | Candidate asymmetry to attack | Orchestrator note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unsettledPot` | Inflow :224 vs `+=` :233 — same amount? Both exits zero it fully | No asymmetry seen; check every path that can reach a terminal state without passing either exit |
| `remainingRefundLiability` | `-=` :368 must equal Σ burned ranges × price; underflow would brick last refunder | Holds only if no ticket range is refunded twice / no ticket burned elsewhere first |
| `winnerProceeds` | written only in CashWon branch :548; zeroed only in CashWon redeem :341 | NftWon writes nothing (intended 0) |
| **Cross-asset coupling** | NftWon: `sponsorProceeds` (95%) becomes claimable at settlement :554 and is released :375 with NO dependency on the NFT leg :334 ever succeeding. CashWon/Refunding: prize leg :404 independent of USDC legs | No state converts an undeliverable NFT into cash/refund. DESIGN.md: "arbitrary prize contracts … are untrusted"; I:14-15 says "Supported prizes are honest, standards-compliant ERC-721s" — conflicting trust statements |
| Ticket screen vs payout screen | `_update` :498 screens recipients when a ticket moves; `_transferQuote` :565 re-screens at payout. `isRaffle` is only queried when `code.length != 0` :602 | Time-of-check vs time-of-use: a destination that is safe at transfer may be "unsafe" at payout (and vice-versa) |
| Native ETH | `msg.value` in, `requestPrice` + excess out; forced ETH unaccounted | `paidPrice` and `quotedFee` both computed from `tx.gasprice` in the same tx |

## 4. Invariants (D = from DESIGN.md, C = derived from code)

1. C: `USDC.balanceOf(raffle) >= accountedQuoteBalance()` at every step (solvency).
2. C: pre-terminal, `unsettledPot == totalEntries * 1e6 == Σ tickets (last-first+1) * 1e6`.
3. C: in Refunding, `remainingRefundLiability == Σ unburned tickets × 1e6`; the last refunder is paid in full.
4. D: NftWon → NFT to winner, 95% sponsor / 5% treasury. CashWon → 80% gross to winner, 15% sponsor, 5% treasury. Refunding → 100% per entry + prize returned.
5. D: fee floors on the aggregate; remainder allocated without loss (`cash + sponsor + fee == pot`).
6. C: ranges are contiguous, disjoint, cover `[1,totalEntries]`; exactly one ticket contains `winningEntry ∈ [1,totalEntries]`, and that ticket exists unburned at settlement.
7. D/C: the prize leaves exactly once — to the winner iff NftWon, to `sponsorRecipient` iff CashWon or Refunding.
8. C: each ticket is paid at most once (refund XOR winning redemption).
9. C: status is monotone `AwaitingPrize→Active→[Drawing→]{NftWon|CashWon|Refunding}`; terminal states never change; NftWon/CashWon can never reach Refunding.
10. D: request window `[endTime, endTime+2d)`; callback accepted strictly before `drawRequestedAt+2d`; refunds open at the deadline — callback and refund windows are disjoint.
11. D: callback records the result only; settlement is permissionless and storage-only.
12. D: redemption requires the CURRENT ticket owner, burns atomically, and reverts all effects on delivery failure.
13. D: sponsor and treasury claim independently after settlement.
14. D: never move assets between raffle clones; payouts never land on protocol plumbing.
15. C (liveness): every party with a claim (refunder, winner, sponsorRecipient, treasury) can always eventually collect it; no reachable state strands USDC or the NFT for its rightful owner.

## 5. Lifecycles (state touched per step)

- **L1 Create**: `F:createRaffle` → `F:_validateCreateParams` (prize code, ERC-165, recipient screen, `reserveEntries>0`) → `Clones.clone` → `initialize` (sponsor, recipient, treasury, prize, id, reserve, endTime; `AwaitingPrize`) → `raffleById/idByRaffle/isRaffle` → `prize.safeTransferFrom` (untrusted code runs) → `onERC721Received` (`Active`) → `ownerOf` + `status` checks.
- **L2 Sale** `[create, endTime)`: `buyEntries` → USDC in, `totalEntries`, `ticketCount`, `_ticketRanges`, `unsettledPot`, `_safeMint` (recipient code runs, `nonReentrant`).
- **L3 Draw OK**: `requestDraw` (`Drawing`, `drawRequestedAt`, `_requestInFlight`, `vrfRequestId`, ETH out + excess refund call) → wrapper `rawFulfillRandomWords` → `fulfillRandomWords` (`winningEntry`, `resolvedAt`, `NftWon|CashWon`) → `settleWinningTicket` (split, `unsettledPot=0`) → `redeemWinningTicket` (burn; NFT or cash) → `releaseSponsorProceeds` / `releaseProtocolFees` → CashWon: `releaseSponsorPrize`.
- **L4 Draw fails**: `requestDraw` → no / late / ignored callback → `enableRefunds` (Drawing branch, ≥ `callbackDeadline()`) → `refundTickets`×k → `releaseSponsorPrize`.
- **L5 No draw**: sold raffle, nobody calls `requestDraw` in 2 days → `enableRefunds` (Active branch, ≥ `drawRequestDeadline()`) → refunds → prize back.
- **L6 Empty**: `totalEntries==0` → sponsor `enableRefunds` any time, anyone after `endTime` → `releaseSponsorPrize`.
- **L7 Ticket market**: transfer in any state via `_update` screen; whoever owns at redeem/refund time is paid; approved operators cannot redeem/refund (owner-only :321, :360).
- **L8 Redeem-with-settle**: `redeemWinningTicket` on an unsettled raffle calls `_settleWinningTicket` itself :315.

## 6. Cohorts (who is owed what)

- **Sponsor** (`msg.sender` of `createRaffle`): escrows the NFT; may cancel an empty raffle early; may also buy entries (can move `totalEntries` across `reserveEntries`).
- **sponsorRecipient** (immutable): `sponsorProceeds` + returned NFT.
- **Protocol treasury** (factory immutable): 5% fee on any settled outcome; 0 on refunds.
- **Buyers / ticket holders**: pay `n × 1e6`; owed 100% back in Refunding; otherwise only the winner is owed.
- **Winner** = owner of the winning ticket at redemption: NFT (NftWon) or 80% of pot (CashWon). No redemption deadline.
- **Last buyer before `endTime`**: knows `totalEntries` and decides whether the reserve is met.
- **Draw requester** (anyone): pays the native VRF fee, never reimbursed. **Settler / releaser** (anyone): unpaid.
- **Trusted**: USDC, Chainlink VRF v2.5 native wrapper. **Untrusted** (DESIGN.md): prize contract (gets control at F:128, F:129, :334-335, :404-405), ticket recipients (`_safeMint` :235, ticket `safeTransferFrom`), excess-ETH refund recipient :267.
- **Not `nonReentrant`**: ERC-721 ticket `transferFrom/safeTransferFrom/approve/setApprovalForAll`, `onERC721Received`, `initialize`, `rawFulfillRandomWords`, views. Every other state-changing raffle function is `nonReentrant`; `F:createRaffle` is `nonReentrant` on the factory only.

## 7. Timing table (exclusive upper bounds)

| Action | Allowed when |
| --- | --- |
| `buyEntries` | `Active` and `now < endTime` :216 |
| `requestDraw` | `Active`, `now >= endTime`, `totalEntries>0`, `now < endTime+2d` :241-247 |
| callback resolves | `Drawing`, matching id, 1 word, not in-flight, `now < drawRequestedAt+2d` :510-513 |
| `enableRefunds` | Active+sold: `now >= endTime+2d`; Drawing: `now >= drawRequestedAt+2d`; Active+empty: sponsor any time, others `now >= endTime` :279-294 |
| settle / redeem | `NftWon` or `CashWon`, no deadline |
| `releaseSponsorPrize` | `CashWon` or `Refunding`, once |

1540	### DESIGN.md (in-scope clean specification)
1541	
1542	```markdown
1543	# Clean design specification
1544	Ethereum NFT raffle; immutable factory, ERC-1167 clones with immutable implementation. One entry costs 1,000,000 units of canonical six-decimal USDC. One purchase mints a transferable ERC721 ticket representing a contiguous inclusive range. Exactly one ERC721 prize is escrowed atomically at creation. Reserve met awards NFT and 95% sponsor / 5% treasury. Reserve missed awards 80% gross to winner, 15% sponsor, 5% treasury. Refund outcome pays 100% per entry and returns prize. Rounding is floor on aggregate protocol fee; remainder must be allocated without loss. No administrator, mutable configuration or upgrade. Request window [sale end, end+2days); callback accepted strictly before request timestamp+2days. Refunds open at deadline. Callback records result only. Settlement is permissionless, storage-only; redemption requires current ticket owner, burns claim atomically, and must revert all effects on delivery failure. Sponsor and treasury can claim independently after settlement. Never move assets between raffle clones. Quote token and Chainlink wrapper are trusted canonical dependencies; arbitrary prize contracts and ticket recipients are untrusted. Frontend discovery is advisory; transaction decisions must reread current chain state.
1545	
1546	This specification was composed before scanner results and historical findings. Source, not design prose, determines actual behavior. No tests, audit history, accepted-risk lists or scanner results are provided.
1547	```

DESIGN.md: "arbitrary prize contracts … are untrusted"; I:14-15 says "Supported prizes are honest, standards-compliant ERC-721s" — conflicting trust statements |

1596	## 4. Invariants (D = from DESIGN.md, C = derived from code)
1597	
1598	1. C: `USDC.balanceOf(raffle) >= accountedQuoteBalance()` at every step (solvency).
1599	2. C: pre-terminal, `unsettledPot == totalEntries * 1e6 == Σ tickets (last-first+1) * 1e6`.

1600	3. C: in Refunding, `remainingRefundLiability == Σ unburned tickets × 1e6`; the last refunder is paid in full.
1601	4. D: NftWon → NFT to winner, 95% sponsor / 5% treasury. CashWon → 80% gross to winner, 15% sponsor, 5% treasury. Refunding → 100% per entry + prize returned.
1602	5. D: fee floors on the aggregate; remainder allocated without loss (`cash + sponsor + fee == pot`).
1603	6. C: ranges are contiguous, disjoint, cover `[1,totalEntries]`; exactly one ticket contains `winningEntry ∈ [1,totalEntries]`, and that ticket exists unburned at settlement.
1604	7. D/C: the prize leaves exactly once — to the winner iff NftWon, to `sponsorRecipient` iff CashWon or Refunding.
1605	8. C: each ticket is paid at most once (refund XOR winning redemption).
1606	9. C: status is monotone `AwaitingPrize→Active→[Drawing→]{NftWon|CashWon|Refunding}`; terminal states never change; NftWon/CashWon can never reach Refunding.
1607	10. D: request window `[endTime, endTime+2d)`; callback accepted strictly before `drawRequestedAt+2d`; refunds open at the deadline — callback and refund windows are disjoint.
1608	11. D: callback records the result only; settlement is permissionless and storage-only.
1609	12. D: redemption requires the CURRENT ticket owner, burns atomically, and reverts all effects on delivery failure.
1610	13. D: sponsor and treasury claim independently after settlement.
1611	14. D: never move assets between raffle clones; payouts never land on protocol plumbing.
1612	15. C (liveness): every party with a claim (refunder, winner, sponsorRecipient, treasury) can always eventually collect it; no reachable state strands USDC or the NFT for its rightful owner.

1614	## 5. Lifecycles (state touched per step)
1615	
1616	- **L1 Create**: `F:createRaffle` → `F:_validateCreateParams` (prize code, ERC-165, recipient screen, `reserveEntries>0`) → `Clones.clone` → `initialize` (sponsor, recipient, treasury, prize, id, reserve, endTime; `AwaitingPrize`) → `raffleById/idByRaffle/isRaffle` → `prize.safeTransferFrom` (untrusted code runs) → `onERC721Received` (`Active`) → `ownerOf` + `status` checks.
1617	- **L2 Sale** `[create, endTime)`: `buyEntries` → USDC in, `totalEntries`, `ticketCount`, `_ticketRanges`, `unsettledPot`, `_safeMint` (recipient code runs, `nonReentrant`).
1618	- **L3 Draw OK**: `requestDraw` (`Drawing`, `drawRequestedAt`, `_requestInFlight`, `vrfRequestId`, ETH out + excess refund call) → wrapper `rawFulfillRandomWords` → `fulfillRandomWords` (`winningEntry`, `resolvedAt`, `NftWon|CashWon`) → `settleWinningTicket` (split, `unsettledPot=0`) → `redeemWinningTicket` (burn; NFT or cash) → `releaseSponsorProceeds` / `releaseProtocolFees` → CashWon: `releaseSponsorPrize`.
1619	- **L4 Draw fails**: `requestDraw` → no / late / ignored callback → `enableRefunds` (Drawing branch, ≥ `callbackDeadline()`) → `refundTickets`×k → `releaseSponsorPrize`.
1620	- **L5 No draw**: sold raffle, nobody calls `requestDraw` in 2 days → `enableRefunds` (Active branch, ≥ `drawRequestDeadline()`) → refunds → prize back.
1621	- **L6 Empty**: `totalEntries==0` → sponsor `enableRefunds` any time, anyone after `endTime` → `releaseSponsorPrize`.
1622	- **L7 Ticket market**: transfer in any state via `_update` screen; whoever owns at redeem/refund time is paid; approved operators cannot redeem/refund (owner-only :321, :360).
1623	- **L8 Redeem-with-settle**: `redeemWinningTicket` on an unsettled raffle calls `_settleWinningTicket` itself :315.

1625	## 6. Cohorts (who is owed what)
1626	
1627	- **Sponsor** (`msg.sender` of `createRaffle`): escrows the NFT; may cancel an empty raffle early; may also buy entries (can move `totalEntries` across `reserveEntries`).
1628	- **sponsorRecipient** (immutable): `sponsorProceeds` + returned NFT.
1629	- **Protocol treasury** (factory immutable): 5% fee on any settled outcome; 0 on refunds.
1630	- **Buyers / ticket holders**: pay `n × 1e6`; owed 100% back in Refunding; otherwise only the winner is owed.
1631	- **Winner** = owner of the winning ticket at redemption: NFT (NftWon) or 80% of pot (CashWon). No redemption deadline.
1632	- **Last buyer before `endTime`**: knows `totalEntries` and decides whether the reserve is met.
1633	- **Draw requester** (anyone): pays the native VRF fee, never reimbursed. **Settler / releaser** (anyone): unpaid.
1634	- **Trusted**: USDC, Chainlink VRF v2.5 native wrapper. **Untrusted** (DESIGN.md): prize contract (gets control at F:128, F:129, :334-335, :404-405), ticket recipients (`_safeMint` :235, ticket `safeTransferFrom`), excess-ETH refund recipient :267.
1635	- **Not `nonReentrant`**: ERC-721 ticket `transferFrom/safeTransferFrom/approve/setApprovalForAll`, `onERC721Received`, `initialize`, `rawFulfillRandomWords`, views. Every other state-changing raffle function is `nonReentrant`; `F:createRaffle` is `nonReentrant` on the factory only.

1647	# The 0xSimao Method
1648	
1649	Derived from 869 published findings across 143 reviews. This is HOW to think. Your lens file is WHAT to look for. Work them together.
1650	
1651	## The core thesis
1652	
1653	Most auditors read code looking for bad lines. That finds the bugs a linter finds.
1654	
1655	0xSimao reads code looking for **a claim that has drifted from what actually backs it**. Value moves through a protocol in sequences: deposit, accrue, borrow, liquidate, withdraw. Each step writes some subset of the accounting state, and drift is any way that state stops describing reality:
1656	
1657	| Drift | Shape |
1658	| --- | --- |
1659	| The write is missing | value moved and no variable recorded it — or one branch updates it and the sibling branch does not |
1660	| The write is wrong | the variable is updated with the wrong amount, direction, rounding, units, or decimals |
1661	| The write is mistimed | the right value at the wrong moment, so someone's snapshot is taken against state that is about to change |
1662	| The write goes to the wrong party | the total is intact; the split between cohorts is not |
1663	| The input was never trustworthy | the number is faithfully propagated from an oracle, a live balance, or a caller-supplied parameter an attacker controls |
1664	| The state is unreachable | the accounting is correct but a revert, a pause, an unbounded loop, or a missing path means it can never be settled |
1665	
1666	The drift is invisible at any single line. It only appears when you ask: *after this whole sequence, does the protocol still owe exactly what it holds — and can everyone actually collect it?*
1667	
1668	A defect nobody can be shown to lose money from is a curiosity. So every candidate gets one more question, and it is the one that separates a finding from a smell:
1669	
1670	> **Who is left holding the loss?**
1671	
1672	Answer with a named class of actor, never "users". For accounting drift it is often whoever withdraws last, because a shortfall stays invisible until the balance runs out — but for a bricked liquidation it is the solvent lenders eating the bad debt, for a mistimed snapshot it is the cohort that held through the accrual, and for a forged signature it is whoever the forged message was drawn against. If the only person worse off is the caller, there is no finding.
1673	
1674	**This lens is the sharpest one, not the only one.** Accounting drift is the largest single class in his corpus, but it is not the majority of it. The rest is DoS and permanently stuck funds, access control and signature defects, token- and integration-behaviour assumptions (`USDT` approvals, fee-on-transfer, blacklists, pausable collateral), oracle and parameter validation, and cross-chain state — and those are what your lens file owns. Work the money map first because it is what makes the drift class visible; then work your lens on its own terms. When the target has little accounting to speak of — a router, a registry, a verifier, a signature scheme — say so, keep the money map short, and go straight to your lens. Do not force a finding into the drift frame to make it sound like his.
1675	
1676	## Phase 0 — Learn the protocol's own vocabulary before reading for bugs
1677	
1678	His findings are written in the protocol's language: `cdsPoolValue`, `abond`, `downsideProtected`, `unassignedEarnings`, `raBalance`, `floatingBackupBorrowed`. He does not audit "a vault"; he audits *this* vault's specific accounting model.
1679	
1680	Before hunting, be able to state in plain English:
1681	- What does a user give, and what claim do they receive in return?
1682	- What is that claim worth, and which variables determine the value?
1683	- Where does yield come from, and who is entitled to it?
1684	- What happens when the protocol is short — who absorbs the shortfall?
1685	
1686	If you cannot answer these without Solidity jargon, you are not ready to find his class of bug. Any spot where your plain-English explanation goes fuzzy is exactly where the bug is; mark it and come back.
1687	
1688	## Phase 1 — Build the money map
1689	
1690	For every storage variable that claims to be an aggregate — `total*`, `*Supply`, `*Balance`, `*Deposited`, `*Locked`, `*Reserve`, `*Debt`, `*Accrued`, indices, cumulative rates — enumerate **every** function that writes it and whether that write increases or decreases it.
1691	
1692	Then build the asymmetry table. Three columns of pure gold:
1693	
1694	| Asymmetry | What to look for | Real finding |
1695	| --- | --- | --- |
1696	| Moved without tracking | value transferred out with no matching decrement | *"Users redeeming early will withdraw `Ra` without decreasing the amount locked, which will lead to stolen funds when withdrawing after expiry"* |
1697	| Tracked in one branch only | `if` updates the total, `else` does not | *"Users will steal excess funds from the Vault due to `VaultPoolLib::redeem()` not always decreasing `raBalance` and `paBalance`"* |
1698	| Never tracked at all | a balance is real but no variable represents it | *"Total `ETH`, `WETH` and `gameETH` are not tracked which will lead to insolvency"* |
1699	
1700	Also flag every place a **live balance read** (`token.balanceOf(address(this))`, `address(this).balance`) is used as an accounting source. That is a donation attack or a cross-user theft waiting to happen — *"`ManagedLeveragedVault::openDen()` using all `asset()` balance"*, *"SDAIPriceFeed is vulnerable to donation attack via manipulatable vault rate"*.
1701	
1702	## Phase 2 — Write the invariants down
1703	
1704	5–15 statements that must always hold. Concretely, not vaguely:
1705	
1706	- `Σ(all user withdrawable) <= actual token balance` — the solvency invariant, his single most productive one
1707	- `totalX == Σ userX` for every aggregate with a per-user counterpart
1708	- every credited unit is debited exactly once, in exactly one place
1709	- monotonic things (indices, cumulative rates, timestamps) never go backwards and cannot be advanced for free
1710	- a user's claim cannot increase from an action that costs them nothing
1711	- state on chain A and chain B agree after every message settles
1712	
1713	An invariant you can state and then break with a sequence is a finding. An invariant the docs assert and the code does not enforce is his highest-yield source of all.
1714	
1715	## Phase 3 — Run the lifecycles, not the functions
1716	
1717	Do not audit function by function. Audit *sequences*, and after each step write down which accounting variables changed and which should have.
1718	
1719	Canonical sequences to run:
1720	
1721	1. deposit → accrue yield → withdraw
1722	2. deposit → borrow → price moves → liquidate → withdraw
1723	3. stake → rewards distributed → unstake → claim
1724	4. deposit → withdraw → deposit again (re-entry into the same accounting slot — *"Borrower deposit, withdraw, deposit will reinit `omniChainData.cdsPoolValue`"*)
1725	5. open → adjust position → close (does the adjust path keep every invariant the open path established? — *"The health of a `ProtectedListing` is incorrectly calculated if `tokenTaken` has been changed through `adjustPosition()`"*)
1726	6. source chain send → destination chain receive → failure/retry
1727	7. the same sequence at expiry / after maturity / after the vault has ended
1728	
1729	For each, ask at every step: **what did we just change that something else still assumes the old value of?**
1730	
1731	## Phase 4 — Attack across cohorts and across time
1732	
1733	This is the most distinctive part of his method, and the least commonly imitated.
1734	
1735	Value in DeFi is split pro-rata among a changing set of holders. Any calculation that uses a *current* total to distribute a *historically accumulated* amount lets someone join late and take a share of value they did not earn.
1736	
1737	Three questions, applied to every distribution, reward, fee, yield, and profit path:
1738	
1739	1. **Can I join immediately before a distribution and take a share of it?**
1740	   *"Immediately start getting rewards belonging to others after staking"*, *"Late abond holders steal USDa amount from liquidations from earlier abond holders"*, *"increaseNetworkTotal() allows big arbitrage opportunities by depositing before an increase transaction"*
1741	2. **Can I leave immediately before a loss and push it onto whoever stays?**
1742	   *"Borrower withdrawing at a loss will cause losses for cds depositors that only withdraw after the price recovers"*
1743	3. **The Last User Out test.** Have every user withdraw, in sequence, in the worst order. Does the last one get paid? If the protocol is short by even dust, the money map has a leak upstream — go find it.
1744	   *"`totalEarnings` is incorrect when withdrawing after ending which will withdraw too many funds leaving the `Vault` insolvent"*
1745	
1746	Cumulative-rate and index-based accounting deserves special hostility: check whether the index can be advanced without cost (*"Malicious user can call `calculateCumulativeRate()` any number of times to inflate debt rate as `lastEventTime` is not updated"*), and whether a user's snapshot is taken at the right moment (*"Depositing to another receiver other than `msg.sender` will lead to stuck funds by increasing `avgStart` without claiming"*).
1747	
1748	## Phase 5 — Saturate the subsystem
1749	
1750	When you find one bug, **do not move on**. His reports cluster: 38 findings in one protocol, most in a single accounting subsystem. That is not luck. Once the accounting model is in your head, mine it out.
1751	
1752	After every finding:
1753	1. Search the codebase for every other site with the same code shape — by function name *and* by pattern. If `redeem()` forgets a decrement, check `withdraw()`, `emergencyWithdraw()`, `redeemExpired()`, and the cross-chain variant.
1754	2. Attack the other branches of the function where you found it.
1755	3. Escalate: a DoS often conceals fund theft; a rounding error often compounds into drain. Push each finding to its worst exploitable variant before writing it up.
1756	
1757	A repeat instance you missed is an audit failure, not an omission.
1758	
1759	## Phase 6 — Prove it, with preconditions stated honestly
1760	
1761	His writeups make the reader's job trivial by separating what the protocol must look like from what the world must look like:
1762	
1763	- **Internal pre-conditions** — protocol state required (a maturity exists, a position is near liquidation, deposits are non-zero). "None" is common and is the strongest possible case.
1764	- **External pre-conditions** — market/oracle/chain conditions required (price moves X%, sequencer down, gas above Y). "None" is again the strongest case.
1765	- **Attack path** — numbered, concrete, with actors and numbers. Not "an attacker could manipulate the rate" but "1. User deposits 100e18. 2. User is liquidated via `liquidationType1()`, adding 5e18 USDa. 3. Attacker deposits via flashloan and withdraws, taking 4.9e18 of it."
1766	- **Impact** — who loses what. Name the victim class.
1767	
1768	If you cannot fill the attack path with real numbers, you have a LEAD. Say so. A well-described lead is worth more than a finding you inflated.
1769	
1770	## Phase 7 — Minimal mitigation
1771	
1772	One change, the smallest that removes the defect, stated in the protocol's own terms:
1773	
1774	- "Add a cumulative tracking variable to handle this case."
1775	- "Set the vesting interest to 0 when the new interest is 0."
1776	- "Decrease `raBalance` in the early-redemption branch as well."
1777	- "Use `mulDiv` when converting between token and share amounts."
1778	
1779	Not "refactor the accounting system." Not "consider adding validation." Name the operation to add, remove, or reorder.
1780	
1781	## Three habits that separate his findings from noise
1782	
1783	**Root cause is a missing operation at a named line.** Very often the bug is not a wrong line but an absent one. Write it that way: *"In `PsmLib.sol:125`, `self.psm.balances.ra.decLocked(amount)` is not called."* Pointing at the absence is what makes the fix obvious.
1784	
1785	**Judge what the code allows, never what the deployer intends.** "The admin wouldn't do that" is not a mitigation. But equally, "admin can rug" with no concrete mechanism is not a finding.
1786	
1787	**Doubt the clean-looking path hardest.** The functions that read as obviously correct are the ones everyone else also skipped. When a guard looks sufficient, name three specific ways to defeat it — with addresses, values, and states, not abstractions — before you accept it.
1788	
1789	## Do not report
1790	
1791	Admin-only functions doing admin things. Standard, accepted DeFi tradeoffs (ordinary MEV on a swap the user chose, rounding dust with no amplification, first-depositor inflation where `MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY` or a virtual-share offset is already present). Self-harm-only bugs. "Centralization risk" with no mechanism. Gas optimizations dressed as vulnerabilities. Missing zero-address checks on admin setters.
1792	# Lens 1 — Accounting Desync
1793	
1794	You own the single largest class of 0xSimao's High findings: **a tracked total that no longer equals the thing it claims to track.**
1795	
1796	Other lenses own math, ordering, and access. You own the gap between what the protocol *records* and what it *holds*.
1797	
1798	## The shape
1799	
1800	Value moves. A variable is supposed to move with it. It does not — or it moves in one branch and not the other, or it is written before the math that depends on its old value, or it is reinitialized when it should have accumulated.
1801	
1802	Everyone downstream then computes against a lie. Early actors withdraw more than they are owed. The protocol becomes short. The last user out cannot be paid.
1803	
1804	## Attack surfaces
1805	
1806	**Hunt the missing decrement.** For every transfer out, find the variable that should have decreased. If none exists, or if the decrement lives in only one of several exit paths, you have it. Check `withdraw`, `redeem`, `emergencyWithdraw`, `claim`, expiry paths, liquidation paths, and cross-chain variants — the forgotten one is rarely the main path.
1807	> *Users redeeming early will withdraw `Ra` without decreasing the amount locked, which will lead to stolen funds when withdrawing after expiry*
1808	> *Missing Update to `omnichain.totalAvailableLiquidationAmount` in `withdrawUser`*
1809	> *Method refundPlayers doesn't update `_lockedETH` in WinnableTicketManager*
1810	
1811	**Hunt the one-sided branch.** Any `if`/`else` where one branch writes an accounting variable and the other does not. Any early `return` that skips a write. Any `try`/`catch` where the failure path leaves state half-updated.
1812	> *Users will steal excess funds from the Vault due to `VaultPoolLib::redeem()` not always decreasing `raBalance` and `paBalance`*
1813	
1814	**Hunt write-before-read.** A variable mutated before the calculation that needed its pre-state. Burning shares before computing share value inflates the price for the burner. Transferring before setting a rate distributes at the wrong rate.
1815	> *`burnSharesToWithdrawEarnings` burns before math, causing the share value to increase*
1816	> *`Voter::finalize()` incorrect rewards distribution due to transferring WETH before calling `distributor::setTokensPerInterval()`*
1817	
1818	**Hunt the untracked balance.** A token or ETH balance that is real but has no variable representing it, or is represented by `balanceOf(address(this))`. Live balance reads are donatable and shared across users.
1819	> *Total `ETH`, `WETH` and `gameETH` are not tracked which will lead to insolvency*
1820	> *Lost withdrawals due to `ManagedLeveragedVault::openDen()` using all `asset()` balance*
1821	> *Incorrect withdraw queue balance in TVL calculation*
1822	
1823	**Hunt the reinitialization.** State that should accumulate but gets overwritten when a user re-enters. Run deposit → withdraw → deposit on every position-holding structure and check whether the second deposit resets something the first established.
1824	> *Borrower deposit, withdraw, deposit will reinit `omniChainData.cdsPoolValue`, getting profit stuck for cds depositors*
1825	> *Cancelling rounds after finalizing will lead to incorrect `globalTokenAllocPerIDORound` tracking*
1826	
1827	**Hunt the mismatched pair.** Two amounts that must be equal but are computed differently — burn `newAmount` but redeem `amount`, debit from `msg.sender` but read state from `user`, credit shares from one formula and debit from another.
1828	> *`BasicVault::_redeem()` burns newAmount but redeems amount, allowing attackers to drain the vault*
1829	> *`Borrowing::redeemYields` debits `ABOND` from `msg.sender` but redeems to `user` using `ABOND.State` data from `user`*
1830	> *Mismatch between yield amount deposited in shares calculation and `getAccountYieldBalance()`*
1831	
1832	**Hunt the unreturned value.** A function returns the actual amount moved and the caller ignores it, assuming the requested amount. Fee-on-transfer, partial fills, capped withdrawals, and AMM slippage all make requested ≠ actual.
1833	> *Providing liquidity to the AMM does not check the return value of actually provided tokens leading to locked funds*
1834	> *Fee on transfer tokens transfer less tokens than what is stored in the receipt on deposits*
1835	> *`FlashSwapRouter::emptyReserve()` and `emptyReservePartial()` functions return incorrect values*
1836	
1837	**Hunt value with no owner.** Fees, dust, residuals, and yields that accrue to no one and can be claimed by anyone — or by nobody, permanently.
1838	> *Protocol fee from Market.sol is locked*
1839	> *Yield from LRTs are forever stuck in the protocol and cannot be withdrawn*
1840	> *In the `unlockProtectedListing()` function, the interest that was supposed to be distributed to LP holders was instead burned*
1841	> *Interest generated by last bond will not go to anyone when liquidating as there is no bond amount to collect it*
1842	
1843	## Required closing test
1844	
1845	For every lifecycle in the money map, run `[LastOut: <lifecycle>]`: every user withdraws in the worst possible order. If the protocol is short by any amount, trace back to the step that leaked and report *that*, not the failed withdrawal.
1846	
1847	## Every finding needs the balance sheet
1848	
1849	State the shortfall concretely: after N steps, users can claim X, the contract holds Y, X > Y by Z. No numbers = LEAD.
1850	# Shared Lens Rules
1851	
1852	## Bundle contents
1853	
1854	Your bundle is five concatenated parts: all in-scope source, the protocol's **money map** (built by the orchestrator), the **method** (how to think), your **lens** (what you own), and these shared rules (output format and protocol).
1855	
1856	Read the whole bundle once at the start. Do not re-read in-scope files for the initial scan. Read or search the repo only for cross-file lookups or out-of-scope context (`interfaces/`, `lib/`, `mocks/`, `test/`).
1857	
1858	**Start from the money map, not the file list.** Pick the tracked totals, lifecycles, and cohorts your lens owns, and attack those. The file list is where you go to confirm, not where you begin.
1859	
1860	When matching function names, check both `functionName` and `_functionName` (Solidity convention), and check library variants (`XLib::function`).
1861	
1862	## Public audit-evidence summaries
1863	
1864	Provide concise public audit evidence and final conclusions, with source references. Do not provide private working text, hidden chain-of-thought, or a transcript of internal deliberation. The following labels organize the public report; they are not instructions to reveal private reasoning or to emit intermediate working text before continuing.
1865	
1866	| Evidence category | Public label | Brief report content |
1867	| --- | --- | --- |
1868	| A function moves value or writes a tracked total | `[Model: <name>]` | Summarize what a user gives, what they receive, and the totals changed, citing the relevant function. |
1869	| A non-obvious operation relies on an assumption | `[Why: <file:line>]` | State the relevant assumption and the source evidence establishing it, or identify the unresolved assumption. |
1870	| An access guard or value-moving path is assessed | `[Defeat: <function>]` | Report concise boundary-test or adversarial-case outcomes and the effective guard or uncovered condition; no private deliberation is requested. |
1871	| A lifecycle is assessed | `[LastOut: <lifecycle>]` | State the conservation/liability result and whether all eligible users can receive the amounts owed, with evidence or a clearly identified gap. |
1872	
1873	Use these summaries as public evidence for the audit result. The orchestrator may inventory which evidence categories were covered; it must not request or evaluate private reasoning traces. All remaining lens scope, saturation, finding format, severity, adjudication, proof and reporting rules are unchanged.
1874	
1875	## Saturation is mandatory
1876	
1877	When you find a bug, weaponize the pattern across the entire codebase before moving on. Search by function name AND by code shape. If one redemption path forgets a decrement, check every other redemption, withdrawal, emergency, expiry, and cross-chain variant. Then attack the other branches of the function where you found it. Then escalate the finding to its worst exploitable variant — a DoS often hides fund theft.
1878	
1879	A repeat instance you missed is an audit failure.
1880	
1881	## Do not report
1882	
1883	Admin-only functions doing admin things. Accepted DeFi tradeoffs (ordinary MEV on a user-chosen swap, rounding dust with no amplification path, first-depositor inflation where a virtual-share offset or `MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY` already exists). Self-harm-only bugs. "Centralization risk" or "admin can rug" without a concrete mechanism. Missing zero-address checks on admin setters. Gas findings.

1885	## Output
1886	
1887	FINDINGs have a concrete, unguarded, exploitable path with a named victim. LEADs have a real accounting or logic smell with a partial path. Default to LEAD over dropping — never drop.
1888	
1889	**One vulnerability per block.** Same root cause = one block. Needs a different fix = separate block.

1895	external_pre: market/oracle/chain conditions required, or None
1896	path:
1897	  1. actor does X with concrete amount
1898	  2. state changes to Y
1899	  3. actor does Z

820	
821	/// @title raffle.fun Raffle Interface
822	/// @author heesho
823	/// @notice Defines one autonomous NFT raffle using fixed-price USDC entries and one transferable ERC-721 ticket per
824	///         purchase.
825	/// @dev Ticket IDs are sequential. Each ticket stores one inclusive uint128 entry range and remains a transferable
826	///      bearer claim until its owner atomically burns it for redemption or refund. The immutable quote token is trusted
827	///      canonical six-decimal USDC with standard, non-rebasing, fee-free transfers. Supported prizes are honest,
828	///      standards-compliant ERC-721s.
829	/// @custom:version 1.0.0
830	interface IRaffle {
831	    // Types
832	
833	    /// @notice The single authoritative raffle lifecycle and economic result.
834	    enum Status {
835	        /// @notice The clone is initialized and waiting for the factory to escrow the configured prize.
836	        AwaitingPrize,
837	        /// @notice The prize is escrowed and entry sales or post-sale draw initiation are available.
838	        Active,
839	        /// @notice A Chainlink VRF request was accepted and its callback window is open.
840	        Drawing,
841	        /// @notice The reserve was met and the winning ticket may redeem the prize NFT.
842	        NftWon,
843	        /// @notice The reserve was missed and the winning ticket may redeem its cash allocation.
844	        CashWon,
845	        /// @notice Full ticket refunds are enabled and the sponsor may recover the prize NFT.
846	        Refunding
847	    }
848	
849	    /// @notice Complete clone-specific configuration supplied once by the canonical factory.
850	    /// @param sponsor Prize depositor and empty-raffle cancellation authority.
851	    /// @param sponsorRecipient Immutable recipient of sponsor quote proceeds and any returned prize.
852	    /// @param protocolTreasury Immutable recipient of protocol fees.
853	    /// @param prizeToken Standards-compliant ERC-721 prize contract.
854	    /// @param prizeTokenId Token ID of the prize escrowed by this raffle.
855	    /// @param raffleId One-based canonical factory identifier for this raffle.
856	    /// @param reserveEntries Global raw entry-count threshold selecting the NFT outcome when met or exceeded.
857	    /// @param endTime Unix timestamp, in seconds, at which entry sales end exclusively.
858	    struct RaffleInitParams {
859	        address sponsor;
860	        address sponsorRecipient;
861	        address protocolTreasury;
862	        address prizeToken;
863	        uint256 prizeTokenId;
864	        uint256 raffleId;
865	        uint128 reserveEntries;
866	        uint64 endTime;
867	    }
868	
869	    // Events
870	
871	    /// @notice Emitted when the factory deposits the configured prize and activates the raffle.
872	    /// @param prizeToken ERC-721 contract of the deposited prize.
873	    /// @param prizeTokenId Token ID of the deposited prize.
874	    /// @param sponsor Address that deposited the prize through the factory.
875	    event PrizeDeposited(address indexed prizeToken, uint256 indexed prizeTokenId, address indexed sponsor);
876	
877	    /// @notice Emitted when a buyer pays for entries and one range ticket is minted.
878	    /// @param buyer Address that paid the six-decimal quote-token amount.
879	    /// @param recipient Address that received the newly minted ticket.
880	    /// @param ticketId Sequential ticket ID assigned to the purchase.
881	    /// @param firstEntry First global raffle entry represented by the ticket, inclusive.
882	    /// @param lastEntry Last global raffle entry represented by the ticket, inclusive.
883	    /// @param entryCount Number of entries represented by the ticket.
884	    /// @param grossAmount Raw six-decimal quote-token units paid, equal to `entryCount * ENTRY_PRICE`.
885	    event TicketPurchased(
886	        address indexed buyer,
887	        address indexed recipient,
888	        uint256 indexed ticketId,
889	        uint128 firstEntry,
890	        uint128 lastEntry,
891	        uint128 entryCount,
892	        uint256 grossAmount
893	    );
894	
895	    /// @notice Emitted when the raffle pays for and records its one Chainlink VRF request.
896	    /// @param requestId Wrapper-assigned request identifier.
897	    /// @param requester Address that initiated and funded the request.
898	    /// @param fee Native-token wei actually paid to the wrapper for the request.
899	    /// @param excessReturned Native-token wei returned to the requester after paying the actual fee.
900	    /// @param drawRequestedAt Unix timestamp, in seconds, when the request was accepted.
901	    /// @param callbackDeadline Exclusive Unix-timestamp deadline for accepting the authenticated callback.
902	    event DrawRequested(
903	        uint256 indexed requestId,
904	        address indexed requester,
905	        uint256 fee,
906	        uint256 excessReturned,
907	        uint256 drawRequestedAt,
908	        uint256 callbackDeadline
909	    );
910	
911	    /// @notice Emitted when an authenticated, ABI-decodable callback cannot resolve the raffle.
912	    /// @param receivedRequestId Request ID supplied by the wrapper callback.
913	    /// @param expectedRequestId Request ID currently recorded by the raffle, or zero before request persistence.
914	    /// @param status Current raffle status when the callback is ignored.
915	    event VrfCallbackIgnored(uint256 indexed receivedRequestId, uint256 indexed expectedRequestId, Status status);
916	
917	    /// @notice Emitted when an authenticated callback selects the winning entry and final result.
918	    /// @param requestId Request ID that produced the accepted randomness.
919	    /// @param winningEntry Selected one-based global entry number in `[1,totalEntries]`.
920	    /// @param result Final `NftWon` or `CashWon` result.
921	    event RaffleResolved(uint256 indexed requestId, uint128 indexed winningEntry, Status indexed result);

924	    /// @param finalizer Address that enabled refunds.
925	    /// @param remainingRefundLiability Raw six-decimal quote-token units initially available for ticket refunds.
926	    event RefundsEnabled(address indexed finalizer, uint256 remainingRefundLiability);
927	
928	    /// @notice Emitted when the winning ticket is proven and all terminal quote-token liabilities are allocated.
929	    /// @param ticketId Ticket proven to contain the selected winning entry.
930	    /// @param settler Address that performed permissionless settlement.
931	    /// @param result Final `NftWon` or `CashWon` result.
932	    /// @param cashAmount Raw six-decimal quote-token units allocated to the cash winner; zero for `NftWon`.
933	    /// @param protocolFee Raw six-decimal quote-token units allocated to the treasury, rounded down from gross sales.
934	    /// @param sponsorAmount Raw six-decimal quote-token units allocated to the sponsor recipient as the remainder.
935	    event WinningTicketSettled(

937	        address indexed settler,
938	        Status indexed result,

940	        uint256 protocolFee,

951	    event WinningTicketRedeemed(
952	        uint256 indexed ticketId,
953	        address indexed winner,

956	        address prizeToken,
957	        uint256 prizeTokenId

989	    /// @param prizeToken ERC-721 contract of the returned prize.
990	    /// @param prizeTokenId Token ID of the returned prize.

993	    );

999

1002

1004	    error ZeroAddress();
1005

1015	    error UnexpectedPrize(address token, uint256 tokenId, address from, address operator);

1019	    /// @param currentTime Current block Unix timestamp, in seconds.
1020	    error SaleEnded(uint256 endTime, uint256 currentTime);
1021	
1022	    /// @notice Raised when an entry ticket would be minted to the zero address.
1023	    error InvalidRecipient();
1024	
1025	    /// @notice Raised when a purchase requests no entries.
1026	    error ZeroEntryCount();
1027	
1028	    /// @notice Raised when a purchase would exceed the `uint128` global entry-number representation.
1029	    /// @param totalEntries Current global sold-entry count.
1030	    /// @param requestedEntries Prospective entry count requested by the purchase.
1031	    error TotalEntriesOverflow(uint128 totalEntries, uint128 requestedEntries);
1032	
1033	    /// @notice Raised when a refund batch is empty or exceeds the bounded ticket limit.
1034	    /// @param quantity Number of supplied ticket IDs.
1035	    /// @param maximum Maximum ticket IDs accepted per refund transaction.
1036	    error InvalidTicketBatchSize(uint256 quantity, uint256 maximum);
1037	
1038	    /// @notice Raised when a quote-token claim targets a known protocol destination that could strand the claim.
1039	    /// @param destination Rejected payout recipient.
1040	    error InvalidQuoteDestination(address destination);
1041	
1042	    /// @notice Raised when a draw request is submitted before the sale end.
1043	    /// @param endTime Exclusive sale-end Unix timestamp, in seconds.
1044	    /// @param currentTime Current block Unix timestamp, in seconds.
1045	    error RaffleNotEnded(uint256 endTime, uint256 currentTime);
1046	
1047	    /// @notice Raised when a draw request is submitted at or after the exclusive request deadline.
1048	    /// @param deadline Exclusive draw-request Unix-timestamp deadline, in seconds.
1049	    /// @param currentTime Current block Unix timestamp, in seconds.
1050	    error DrawRequestWindowExpired(uint256 deadline, uint256 currentTime);
1051	
1052	    /// @notice Raised when draw initiation is attempted for a raffle with zero sold entries.
1053	    error NoEntriesSold();
1054	
1055	    /// @notice Raised when refunds are requested before the applicable liveness deadline.
1056	    /// @param deadline Unix timestamp, in seconds, at which refunds become available.
1057	    /// @param currentTime Current block Unix timestamp, in seconds.
1058	    error RefundsNotAvailable(uint256 deadline, uint256 currentTime);
1059	
1060	    /// @notice Raised when supplied native value cannot cover the quoted or actual Chainlink request fee.
1061	    /// @param requiredFee Native-token wei required for the request.
1062	    /// @param suppliedValue Native-token wei supplied by the caller.
1063	    error InsufficientVrfFee(uint256 requiredFee, uint256 suppliedValue);
1064	
1065	    /// @notice Raised when excess native value cannot be returned to the draw requester.
1066	    /// @param recipient Draw requester that was due the refund.
1067	    /// @param amount Native-token wei that could not be returned.
1068	    error NativeRefundFailed(address recipient, uint256 amount);
1069

1071	    error NoWinnerProceeds();
1072	
1073	    /// @notice Raised when no current sponsor proceeds remain claimable.
1074	    error NoSponsorProceeds();
1075	
1076	    /// @notice Raised when no current protocol fees remain claimable.
1077	    error NoProtocolFees();
1078

1080	    /// @param destination Rejected address.

1082

1093

1137	    function enableRefunds() external;
1138	
1139	    /// @notice Proves which ticket contains the winning entry and allocates winner, sponsor, and protocol liabilities.
1140	    /// @dev Anyone may execute; ownership is not read, the ticket remains transferable, and no external asset transfer
1141	    ///      occurs. The cash-winner allocation is rounded down; the sponsor receives the remaining raw units.
1142	    /// @param ticketId Ticket whose stored inclusive range must contain `winningEntry`.
1143	    /// @return cashAmount Raw six-decimal quote-token units allocated to the winner, or zero for an NFT result.
1144	    function settleWinningTicket(uint256 ticketId) external returns (uint256 cashAmount);
1145	
1146	    /// @notice Lets the current winning-ticket owner atomically burn the ticket and receive the NFT or cash prize.
1147	    /// @dev If necessary, this first settles the supplied winning ticket so the owner can complete both steps in one
1148	    ///      transaction. Any failed delivery reverts the burn and every redemption state change.

1151	    function redeemWinningTicket(uint256 ticketId) external returns (uint256 cashAmount);
1152	
1153	    /// @notice Burns an owner-selected batch of tickets and returns their full entry purchase value.

1160	    /// @return amount Raw six-decimal quote-token units paid in this release.
1161	    function releaseSponsorProceeds() external returns (uint256 amount);
1162	
1163	    /// @notice Releases the complete current protocol-fee balance to the immutable treasury.
1164	    /// @return amount Raw six-decimal quote-token units paid in this release.
1165	    function releaseProtocolFees() external returns (uint256 amount);
1166	
1167	    /// @notice Returns the escrowed prize to the immutable sponsor recipient after `CashWon` or `Refunding`.
1168	    function releaseSponsorPrize() external;
1169

1171	
1172	    /// @notice Returns the wrapper's current native direct-funding price for the configured callback.
1173	    /// @return fee Native-token wei currently quoted by the wrapper; the value may change before request inclusion.
1174	    function getVrfRequestPrice() external view returns (uint256 fee);
1175	
1176	    /// @notice Estimates the native direct-funding price at a caller-selected gas price.
1177	    /// @param requestGasPriceWei Prospective transaction gas price in wei per gas.
1178	    /// @return fee Estimated native-token wei for the configured callback and one random word.
1179	    function estimateVrfRequestPrice(uint256 requestGasPriceWei) external view returns (uint256 fee);
1180	
1181	    /// @notice Returns the inclusive global entry range represented by a ticket ID.
1182	    /// @dev Returns zeros for an ID that has never been minted; ranges remain historical after ticket burns.
1183	    /// @param ticketId Sequential ticket ID to inspect.
1184	    /// @return firstEntry First represented one-based global entry, inclusive.
1185	    /// @return lastEntry Last represented one-based global entry, inclusive.
1186	    function ticketRange(uint256 ticketId) external view returns (uint128 firstEntry, uint128 lastEntry);
1187	
1188	    /// @notice Returns the exclusive deadline for initiating the draw.
1189	    /// @return deadline Unix timestamp, in seconds, equal to `endTime + 2 days`.
1190	    function drawRequestDeadline() external view returns (uint256 deadline);
1191

1193	    /// @return deadline Unix timestamp, in seconds, equal to `drawRequestedAt + 2 days`, or zero before a request.
1194	    function callbackDeadline() external view returns (uint256 deadline);

1197	    /// @return amount Raw six-decimal quote-token units across the unsettled pot, refunds, and allocated claims.
1198	    function accountedQuoteBalance() external view returns (uint256 amount);

1543	# Clean design specification
1544	Ethereum NFT raffle; immutable factory, ERC-1167 clones with immutable implementation. One entry costs 1,000,000 units of canonical six-decimal USDC. One purchase mints a transferable ERC721 ticket representing a contiguous inclusive range. Exactly one ERC721 prize is escrowed atomically at creation. Reserve met awards NFT and 95% sponsor / 5% treasury. Reserve missed awards 80% gross to winner, 15% sponsor, 5% treasury. Refund outcome pays 100% per entry and returns prize. Rounding is floor on aggregate protocol fee; remainder must be allocated without loss. No administrator, mutable configuration or upgrade. Request window [sale end, end+2days); callback accepted strictly before request timestamp+2days. Refunds open at deadline. Callback records result only. Settlement is permissionless, storage-only; redemption requires current ticket owner, burns claim atomically, and must revert all effects on delivery failure. Sponsor and treasury can claim independently after settlement. Never move assets between raffle clones. Quote token and Chainlink wrapper are trusted canonical dependencies; arbitrary prize contracts and ticket recipients are untrusted. Frontend discovery is advisory; transaction decisions must reread current chain state.
1545	
1546	This specification was composed before scanner results and historical findings. Source, not design prose, determines actual behavior. No tests, audit history, accepted-risk lists or scanner results are provided.

1543	# Clean design specification
1544	Ethereum NFT raffle; immutable factory, ERC-1167 clones with immutable implementation. One entry costs 1,000,000 units of canonical six-decimal USDC. One purchase mints a transferable ERC721 ticket representing a contiguous inclusive range. Exactly one ERC721 prize is escrowed atomically at creation. Reserve met awards NFT and 95% sponsor / 5% treasury. Reserve missed awards 80% gross to winner, 15% sponsor, 5% treasury. Refund outcome pays 100% per entry and returns prize. Rounding is floor on aggregate protocol fee; remainder must be allocated without loss. No administrator, mutable configuration or upgrade. Request window [sale end, end+2days); callback accepted strictly before request timestamp+2days. Refunds open at deadline. Callback records result only. Settlement is permissionless, storage-only; redemption requires current ticket owner, burns claim atomically, and must revert all effects on delivery failure. Sponsor and treasury can claim independently after settlement. Never move assets between raffle clones. Quote token and Chainlink wrapper are trusted canonical dependencies; arbitrary prize contracts and ticket recipients are untrusted. Frontend discovery is advisory; transaction decisions must reread current chain state.

1647	# The 0xSimao Method
1648	
1649	Derived from 869 published findings across 143 reviews. This is HOW to think. Your lens file is WHAT to look for. Work them together.
1650	
1651	## The core thesis
1652	
1653	Most auditors read code looking for bad lines. That finds the bugs a linter finds.
1654	
1655	0xSimao reads code looking for **a claim that has drifted from what actually backs it**. Value moves through a protocol in sequences: deposit, accrue, borrow, liquidate, withdraw. Each step writes some subset of the accounting state, and drift is any way that state stops describing reality:
1656	
1657	| Drift | Shape |
1658	| --- | --- |
1659	| The write is missing | value moved and no variable recorded it — or one branch updates it and the sibling branch does not |
1660	| The write is wrong | the variable is updated with the wrong amount, direction, rounding, units, or decimals |
1661	| The write is mistimed | the right value at the wrong moment, so someone's snapshot is taken against state that is about to change |
1662	| The write goes to the wrong party | the total is intact; the split between cohorts is not |
1663	| The input was never trustworthy | the number is faithfully propagated from an oracle, a live balance, or a caller-supplied parameter an attacker controls |
1664	| The state is unreachable | the accounting is correct but a revert, a pause, an unbounded loop, or a missing path means it can never be settled |
1665	
1666	The drift is invisible at any single line. It only appears when you ask: *after this whole sequence, does the protocol still owe exactly what it holds — and can everyone actually collect it?*
1667	
1668	A defect nobody can be shown to lose money from is a curiosity. So every candidate gets one more question, and it is the one that separates a finding from a smell:
1669	
1670	> **Who is left holding the loss?**
1671	
1672	Answer with a named class of actor, never "users". For accounting drift it is often whoever withdraws last, because a shortfall stays invisible until the balance runs out — but for a bricked liquidation it is the solvent lenders eating the bad debt, for a mistimed snapshot it is the cohort that held through the accrual, and for a forged signature it is whoever the forged message was drawn against. If the only person worse off is the caller, there is no finding.
1673	
1674	**This lens is the sharpest one, not the only one.** Accounting drift is the largest single class in his corpus, but it is not the majority of it. The rest is DoS and permanently stuck funds, access control and signature defects, token- and integration-behaviour assumptions (`USDT` approvals, fee-on-transfer, blacklists, pausable collateral), oracle and parameter validation, and cross-chain state — and those are what your lens file owns. Work the money map first because it is what makes the drift class visible; then work your lens on its own terms. When the target has little accounting to speak of — a router, a registry, a verifier, a signature scheme — say so, keep the money map short, and go straight to your lens. Do not force a finding into the drift frame to make it sound like his.
1675	
1676	## Phase 0 — Learn the protocol's own vocabulary before reading for bugs
1677	
1678	His findings are written in the protocol's language: `cdsPoolValue`, `abond`, `downsideProtected`, `unassignedEarnings`, `raBalance`, `floatingBackupBorrowed`. He does not audit "a vault"; he audits *this* vault's specific accounting model.
1679	
1680	Before hunting, be able to state in plain English:
1681	- What does a user give, and what claim do they receive in return?
1682	- What is that claim worth, and which variables determine the value?
1683	- Where does yield come from, and who is entitled to it?
1684	- What happens when the protocol is short — who absorbs the shortfall?
1685	
1686	If you cannot answer these without Solidity jargon, you are not ready to find his class of bug. Any spot where your plain-English explanation goes fuzzy is exactly where the bug is; mark it and come back.
1687	
1688	## Phase 1 — Build the money map
1689	
1690	For every storage variable that claims to be an aggregate — `total*`, `*Supply`, `*Balance`, `*Deposited`, `*Locked`, `*Reserve`, `*Debt`, `*Accrued`, indices, cumulative rates — enumerate **every** function that writes it and whether that write increases or decreases it.
1691	
1692	Then build the asymmetry table. Three columns of pure gold:
1693	
1694	| Asymmetry | What to look for | Real finding |
1695	| --- | --- | --- |
1696	| Moved without tracking | value transferred out with no matching decrement | *"Users redeeming early will withdraw `Ra` without decreasing the amount locked, which will lead to stolen funds when withdrawing after expiry"* |
1697	| Tracked in one branch only | `if` updates the total, `else` does not | *"Users will steal excess funds from the Vault due to `VaultPoolLib::redeem()` not always decreasing `raBalance` and `paBalance`"* |
1698	| Never tracked at all | a balance is real but no variable represents it | *"Total `ETH`, `WETH` and `gameETH` are not tracked which will lead to insolvency"* |
1699	
1700	Also flag every place a **live balance read** (`token.balanceOf(address(this))`, `address(this).balance`) is used as an accounting source. That is a donation attack or a cross-user theft waiting to happen — *"`ManagedLeveragedVault::openDen()` using all `asset()` balance"*, *"SDAIPriceFeed is vulnerable to donation attack via manipulatable vault rate"*.
1701	
1702	## Phase 2 — Write the invariants down
1703	
1704	5–15 statements that must always hold. Concretely, not vaguely:
1705	
1706	- `Σ(all user withdrawable) <= actual token balance` — the solvency invariant, his single most productive one
1707	- `totalX == Σ userX` for every aggregate with a per-user counterpart
1708	- every credited unit is debited exactly once, in exactly one place
1709	- monotonic things (indices, cumulative rates, timestamps) never go backwards and cannot be advanced for free
1710	- a user's claim cannot increase from an action that costs them nothing
1711	- state on chain A and chain B agree after every message settles
1712	
1713	An invariant you can state and then break with a sequence is a finding. An invariant the docs assert and the code does not enforce is his highest-yield source of all.
1714	
1715	## Phase 3 — Run the lifecycles, not the functions
1716	
1717	Do not audit function by function. Audit *sequences*, and after each step write down which accounting variables changed and which should have.
1718	
1719	Canonical sequences to run:
1720	
1721	1. deposit → accrue yield → withdraw
1722	2. deposit → borrow → price moves → liquidate → withdraw
1723	3. stake → rewards distributed → unstake → claim
1724	4. deposit → withdraw → deposit again (re-entry into the same accounting slot — *"Borrower deposit, withdraw, deposit will reinit `omniChainData.cdsPoolValue`"*)
1725	5. open → adjust position → close (does the adjust path keep every invariant the open path established? — *"The health of a `ProtectedListing` is incorrectly calculated if `tokenTaken` has been changed through `adjustPosition()`"*)
1726	6. source chain send → destination chain receive → failure/retry
1727	7. the same sequence at expiry / after maturity / after the vault has ended
1728	
1729	For each, ask at every step: **what did we just change that something else still assumes the old value of?**
1730	
1731	## Phase 4 — Attack across cohorts and across time
1732	
1733	This is the most distinctive part of his method, and the least commonly imitated.
1734	
1735	Value in DeFi is split pro-rata among a changing set of holders. Any calculation that uses a *current* total to distribute a *historically accumulated* amount lets someone join late and take a share of value they did not earn.
1736	
1737	Three questions, applied to every distribution, reward, fee, yield, and profit path:
1738	
1739	1. **Can I join immediately before a distribution and take a share of it?**
1740	   *"Immediately start getting rewards belonging to others after staking"*, *"Late abond holders steal USDa amount from liquidations from earlier abond holders"*, *"increaseNetworkTotal() allows big arbitrage opportunities by depositing before an increase transaction"*
1741	2. **Can I leave immediately before a loss and push it onto whoever stays?**
1742	   *"Borrower withdrawing at a loss will cause losses for cds depositors that only withdraw after the price recovers"*
1743	3. **The Last User Out test.** Have every user withdraw, in sequence, in the worst order. Does the last one get paid? If the protocol is short by even dust, the money map has a leak upstream — go find it.
1744	   *"`totalEarnings` is incorrect when withdrawing after ending which will withdraw too many funds leaving the `Vault` insolvent"*
1745	
1746	Cumulative-rate and index-based accounting deserves special hostility: check whether the index can be advanced without cost (*"Malicious user can call `calculateCumulativeRate()` any number of times to inflate debt rate as `lastEventTime` is not updated"*), and whether a user's snapshot is taken at the right moment (*"Depositing to another receiver other than `msg.sender` will lead to stuck funds by increasing `avgStart` without claiming"*).
1747	
1748	## Phase 5 — Saturate the subsystem
1749	
1750	When you find one bug, **do not move on**. His reports cluster: 38 findings in one protocol, most in a single accounting subsystem. That is not luck. Once the accounting model is in your head, mine it out.
1751	
1752	After every finding:
1753	1. Search the codebase for every other site with the same code shape — by function name *and* by pattern. If `redeem()` forgets a decrement, check `withdraw()`, `emergencyWithdraw()`, `redeemExpired()`, and the cross-chain variant.
1754	2. Attack the other branches of the function where you found it.
1755	3. Escalate: a DoS often conceals fund theft; a rounding error often compounds into drain. Push each finding to its worst exploitable variant before writing it up.
1756	
1757	A repeat instance you missed is an audit failure, not an omission.
1758	
1759	## Phase 6 — Prove it, with preconditions stated honestly
1760	
1761	His writeups make the reader's job trivial by separating what the protocol must look like from what the world must look like:
1762	
1763	- **Internal pre-conditions** — protocol state required (a maturity exists, a position is near liquidation, deposits are non-zero). "None" is common and is the strongest possible case.
1764	- **External pre-conditions** — market/oracle/chain conditions required (price moves X%, sequencer down, gas above Y). "None" is again the strongest case.
1765	- **Attack path** — numbered, concrete, with actors and numbers. Not "an attacker could manipulate the rate" but "1. User deposits 100e18. 2. User is liquidated via `liquidationType1()`, adding 5e18 USDa. 3. Attacker deposits via flashloan and withdraws, taking 4.9e18 of it."
1766	- **Impact** — who loses what. Name the victim class.
1767	
1768	If you cannot fill the attack path with real numbers, you have a LEAD. Say so. A well-described lead is worth more than a finding you inflated.
1769	
1770	## Phase 7 — Minimal mitigation
1771	
1772	One change, the smallest that removes the defect, stated in the protocol's own terms:
1773	
1774	- "Add a cumulative tracking variable to handle this case."
1775	- "Set the vesting interest to 0 when the new interest is 0."
1776	- "Decrease `raBalance` in the early-redemption branch as well."
1777	- "Use `mulDiv` when converting between token and share amounts."
1778	
1779	Not "refactor the accounting system." Not "consider adding validation." Name the operation to add, remove, or reorder.
1780	
1781	## Three habits that separate his findings from noise
1782	
1783	**Root cause is a missing operation at a named line.** Very often the bug is not a wrong line but an absent one. Write it that way: *"In `PsmLib.sol:125`, `self.psm.balances.ra.decLocked(amount)` is not called."* Pointing at the absence is what makes the fix obvious.
1784	
1785	**Judge what the code allows, never what the deployer intends.** "The admin wouldn't do that" is not a mitigation. But equally, "admin can rug" with no concrete mechanism is not a finding.
1786	
1787	**Doubt the clean-looking path hardest.** The functions that read as obviously correct are the ones everyone else also skipped. When a guard looks sufficient, name three specific ways to defeat it — with addresses, values, and states, not abstractions — before you accept it.
1788	
1789	## Do not report
1790	
1791	Admin-only functions doing admin things. Standard, accepted DeFi tradeoffs (ordinary MEV on a swap the user chose, rounding dust with no amplification, first-depositor inflation where `MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY` or a virtual-share offset is already present). Self-harm-only bugs. "Centralization risk" with no mechanism. Gas optimizations dressed as vulnerabilities. Missing zero-address checks on admin setters.
1792	# Lens 2 — Shares, Exchange Rates & Redemption
1793	
1794	You own the conversion between **claims** (shares, receipt tokens, positions, notes) and **value** (assets). Every deposit mints a claim; every withdrawal burns one. If the two directions disagree by even a little, someone extracts the difference repeatedly.
1795	
1796	## The shape
1797	
1798	The exchange rate is a ratio of two things the protocol tracks. Break either side — inflate the numerator, deflate the denominator, or change one without the other — and mint/redeem become a money pump.
1799	
1800	## Attack surfaces
1801	
1802	**Round-trip every path.** Deposit X, immediately withdraw. Do you get more than X? Do it again in a loop. Any path where a round trip is profitable at zero risk is a drain, and looping makes it critical.
1803	> *DarkPoolAssetManager can be drained by looping over join(), joinSplit() or swap() with only some initial amount*
1804	> *`_rebalanceWithdraw()` mechanism in glAVAX allows arbitrage opportunities by changing the shares/AVAX ratio*
1805	> *REBALANCER_ROLE can drain funds by rebalancing in a loop in the BorrowingVault*
1806	
1807	**Attack the denominator.** The share price divides by a total. Ask what happens when that total is zero, one wei, or donatable. Live balance reads in the denominator are donation attacks.
1808	> *SDAIPriceFeed is vulnerable to donation attack via manipulatable vault rate*
1809	> *`OffchainExchange::swapAmm()` does not validate that `txn.priceX18 > 0`, allowing donation attacks*
1810	> *`state.cumulativeDepositsMultiplierX18` may become 0 or negative, leading to loss of funds*
1811	
1812	**Check burn order against value computation.** Shares burned before the value calculation change the very rate used to pay out. Establish whether the payout uses pre-burn or post-burn supply, and whether that is what the protocol intends.
1813	> *`burnSharesToWithdrawEarnings` burns before math, causing the share value to increase*
1814	> *Incorrect redeemAmount Is Accounted Due To Not Accounting For The Exchange Rate*
1815	
1816	**Verify the ERC4626 contract, if the protocol claims it.** `maxDeposit`/`maxMint`/`maxWithdraw`/`maxRedeem` must reflect real limits including pauses, caps, and mint limits. `preview*` must match the actual result. `withdraw`/`redeem` with no slippage parameter is a real finding when the rate is manipulable between submission and execution.
1817	> *`maxDeposit` doesn't comply with ERC-4626*
1818	> *`VaultV2::withdraw/redeem()` are vulnerable to slippage, so another function could be added to protect users*
1819	> *`ManagedLeveragedVault.sol::deposit()` is missing slippage control*
1820	> *`LenderCommitmentGroup_Smart_test::addPrincipalToCommitmentGroup/burnSharesToWithdrawEarnings()` are vulnerable to slippage attacks*
1821	
1822	**Break the receipt.** Receipt tokens, position NFTs, and notes carry claims. Ask whether transferring one moves the associated rewards/debt correctly, whether it can be redeemed twice, and whether the claim can be separated from the obligation.
1823	> *Reward Token Loss for LPs During NFT Position Transfer*
1824	> *Staked tokens inside FluidLocker can be withdrawn without calling Unstake*
1825	> *`Fluid (SUP)` can be withdrawn from the Locker while the unlock flag is false*
1826	> *Reusing the same rho and pubKey in different deposits leads to lost tokens*
1827	
1828	**Redeem into the wrong state.** Redemption at expiry, after a slash, while paused, mid-epoch, or after another user's redemption has already changed the pool. His richest vein: the redemption function that is correct in the normal case and wrong in exactly one terminal state.
1829	> *Admin new issuance or user calling `Vault::redeemExpiredLv()` after `Psm::redeemWithCt()` will lead to stuck funds when trying to withdraw*
1830	> *Withdrawing all `lv` before expiry will lead to lost funds in the Vault*
1831	> *Withdrawing after a slash event before the vault has ended will decrease `fixedSidestETHOnStartCapacity` by less than it should, so following users will withdraw more than their initial deposit*
1832	
1833	**Follow the token to the wrong recipient.** Redeem to `user` while burning from `msg.sender`, send collateral to the caller instead of the position owner, route fees to a stale address.
1834	> *liquidateDefaultedLoanWithIncentive sends the collateral to the wrong account*
1835	> *Attackers can claim deposits to vaults if users specify the router as receiver and don't withdraw shares after*
1836	
1837	## Every finding needs the arithmetic
1838	
1839	Show the rate before and after with concrete numbers, and the extracted amount per round trip. "The rate can be manipulated" is a LEAD; "1e18 donated moves the rate from 1.00 to 1.05, extracting 4.7e18 over three loops" is a finding.
