1600	3. C: in Refunding, `remainingRefundLiability == Σ unburned tickets × 1e6`; the last refunder is paid in full.
1601	4. D: NftWon → NFT to winner, 95% sponsor / 5% treasury. CashWon → 80% gross to winner, 15% sponsor, 5% treasury. Refunding → 100% per entry + prize returned.
1602	5. D: fee floors on the aggregate; remainder allocated without loss (`cash + sponsor + fee == pot`).
1603	6. C: ranges are contiguous, disjoint, cover `[1,totalEntries]`; exactly one ticket contains `winningEntry ∈ [1,totalEntries]`, and that ticket exists unburned at settlement.
1604	7. D/C: the prize leaves exactly once — to the winner iff NftWon, to `sponsorRecipient` iff CashWon or Refunding.
1605	8. C: each ticket is paid at most once (refund XOR winning redemption).
1606	9. C: status is monotone `AwaitingPrize→Active→[Drawing→]{NftWon|CashWon|Refunding}`; terminal states never change; NftWon/CashWon can never reach Refunding.
1607	10. D: request window `[endTime, endTime+2d)`; callback accepted strictly before `drawRequestedAt+2d`; refunds open at the deadline — callback and refund windows are disjoint.
1608	11. D: callback records the result only; settlement is permissionless and storage-only.
1609	12. D: redemption requires the CURRENT ticket owner, burns atomically, and reverts all effects on delivery failure.
1610	13. D: sponsor and treasury claim independently after settlement.
1611	14. D: never move assets between raffle clones; payouts never land on protocol plumbing.
1612	15. C (liveness): every party with a claim (refunder, winner, sponsorRecipient, treasury) can always eventually collect it; no reachable state strands USDC or the NFT for its rightful owner.
1613	
1614	## 5. Lifecycles (state touched per step)
1615	
1616	- **L1 Create**: `F:createRaffle` → `F:_validateCreateParams` (prize code, ERC-165, recipient screen, `reserveEntries>0`) → `Clones.clone` → `initialize` (sponsor, recipient, treasury, prize, id, reserve, endTime; `AwaitingPrize`) → `raffleById/idByRaffle/isRaffle` → `prize.safeTransferFrom` (untrusted code runs) → `onERC721Received` (`Active`) → `ownerOf` + `status` checks.
1617	- **L2 Sale** `[create, endTime)`: `buyEntries` → USDC in, `totalEntries`, `ticketCount`, `_ticketRanges`, `unsettledPot`, `_safeMint` (recipient code runs, `nonReentrant`).
1618	- **L3 Draw OK**: `requestDraw` (`Drawing`, `drawRequestedAt`, `_requestInFlight`, `vrfRequestId`, ETH out + excess refund call) → wrapper `rawFulfillRandomWords` → `fulfillRandomWords` (`winningEntry`, `resolvedAt`, `NftWon|CashWon`) → `settleWinningTicket` (split, `unsettledPot=0`) → `redeemWinningTicket` (burn; NFT or cash) → `releaseSponsorProceeds` / `releaseProtocolFees` → CashWon: `releaseSponsorPrize`.
1619	- **L4 Draw fails**: `requestDraw` → no / late / ignored callback → `enableRefunds` (Drawing branch, ≥ `callbackDeadline()`) → `refundTickets`×k → `releaseSponsorPrize`.
1620	- **L5 No draw**: sold raffle, nobody calls `requestDraw` in 2 days → `enableRefunds` (Active branch, ≥ `drawRequestDeadline()`) → refunds → prize back.
1621	- **L6 Empty**: `totalEntries==0` → sponsor `enableRefunds` any time, anyone after `endTime` → `releaseSponsorPrize`.
1622	- **L7 Ticket market**: transfer in any state via `_update` screen; whoever owns at redeem/refund time is paid; approved operators cannot redeem/refund (owner-only :321, :360).
1623	- **L8 Redeem-with-settle**: `redeemWinningTicket` on an unsettled raffle calls `_settleWinningTicket` itself :315.
1624	
1625	## 6. Cohorts (who is owed what)
1626	
1627	- **Sponsor** (`msg.sender` of `createRaffle`): escrows the NFT; may cancel an empty raffle early; may also buy entries (can move `totalEntries` across `reserveEntries`).
1628	- **sponsorRecipient** (immutable): `sponsorProceeds` + returned NFT.
1629	- **Protocol treasury** (factory immutable): 5% fee on any settled outcome; 0 on refunds.
1630	- **Buyers / ticket holders**: pay `n × 1e6`; owed 100% back in Refunding; otherwise only the winner is owed.
1631	- **Winner** = owner of the winning ticket at redemption: NFT (NftWon) or 80% of pot (CashWon). No redemption deadline.
1632	- **Last buyer before `endTime`**: knows `totalEntries` and decides whether the reserve is met.
1633	- **Draw requester** (anyone): pays the native VRF fee, never reimbursed. **Settler / releaser** (anyone): unpaid.
1634	- **Trusted**: USDC, Chainlink VRF v2.5 native wrapper. **Untrusted** (DESIGN.md): prize contract (gets control at F:128, F:129, :334-335, :404-405), ticket recipients (`_safeMint` :235, ticket `safeTransferFrom`), excess-ETH refund recipient :267.
1635	- **Not `nonReentrant`**: ERC-721 ticket `transferFrom/safeTransferFrom/approve/setApprovalForAll`, `onERC721Received`, `initialize`, `rawFulfillRandomWords`, views. Every other state-changing raffle function is `nonReentrant`; `F:createRaffle` is `nonReentrant` on the factory only.
1636	
1637	## 7. Timing table (exclusive upper bounds)
1638	
1639	| Action | Allowed when |
1640	| --- | --- |
1641	| `buyEntries` | `Active` and `now < endTime` :216 |
1642	| `requestDraw` | `Active`, `now >= endTime`, `totalEntries>0`, `now < endTime+2d` :241-247 |
1643	| callback resolves | `Drawing`, matching id, 1 word, not in-flight, `now < drawRequestedAt+2d` :510-513 |
1644	| `enableRefunds` | Active+sold: `now >= endTime+2d`; Drawing: `now >= drawRequestedAt+2d`; Active+empty: sponsor any time, others `now >= endTime` :279-294 |
1645	| settle / redeem | `NftWon` or `CashWon`, no deadline |
1646	| `releaseSponsorPrize` | `CashWon` or `Refunding`, once |
1647	# The 0xSimao Method
1648	
1649	Derived from 869 published findings across 143 reviews. This is HOW to think. Your lens file is WHAT to look for. Work them together.
1650	
1651	## The core thesis
1652	
1653	Most auditors read code looking for bad lines. That finds the bugs a linter finds.
1654	
1655	0xSimao reads code looking for **a claim that has drifted from what actually backs it**. Value moves through a protocol in sequences: deposit, accrue, borrow, liquidate, withdraw. Each step writes some subset of the accounting state, and drift is any way that state stops describing reality:
1656	
1657	| Drift | Shape |
1658	| --- | --- |
1659	| The write is missing | value moved and no variable recorded it — or one branch updates it and the sibling branch does not |
1660	| The write is wrong | the variable is updated with the wrong amount, direction, rounding, units, or decimals |
1661	| The write is mistimed | the right value at the wrong moment, so someone's snapshot is taken against state that is about to change |
1662	| The write goes to the wrong party | the total is intact; the split between cohorts is not |
1663	| The input was never trustworthy | the number is faithfully propagated from an oracle, a live balance, or a caller-supplied parameter an attacker controls |
1664	| The state is unreachable | the accounting is correct but a revert, a pause, an unbounded loop, or a missing path means it can never be settled |
1665	
1666	The drift is invisible at any single line. It only appears when you ask: *after this whole sequence, does the protocol still owe exactly what it holds — and can everyone actually collect it?*
1667	
1668	A defect nobody can be shown to lose money from is a curiosity. So every candidate gets one more question, and it is the one that separates a finding from a smell:
1669	
1670	> **Who is left holding the loss?**
1671	
1672	Answer with a named class of actor, never "users". For accounting drift it is often whoever withdraws last, because a shortfall stays invisible until the balance runs out — but for a bricked liquidation it is the solvent lenders eating the bad debt, for a mistimed snapshot it is the cohort that held through the accrual, and for a forged signature it is whoever the forged message was drawn against. If the only person worse off is the caller, there is no finding.
1673	
1674	**This lens is the sharpest one, not the only one.** Accounting drift is the largest single class in his corpus, but it is not the majority of it. The rest is DoS and permanently stuck funds, access control and signature defects, token- and integration-behaviour assumptions (`USDT` approvals, fee-on-transfer, blacklists, pausable collateral), oracle and parameter validation, and cross-chain state — and those are what your lens file owns. Work the money map first because it is what makes the drift class visible; then work your lens on its own terms. When the target has little accounting to speak of — a router, a registry, a verifier, a signature scheme — say so, keep the money map short, and go straight to your lens. Do not force a finding into the drift frame to make it sound like his.
1675	
1676	## Phase 0 — Learn the protocol's own vocabulary before reading for bugs
1677	
1678	His findings are written in the protocol's language: `cdsPoolValue`, `abond`, `downsideProtected`, `unassignedEarnings`, `raBalance`, `floatingBackupBorrowed`. He does not audit "a vault"; he audits *this* vault's specific accounting model.
1679	
1680	Before hunting, be able to state in plain English:
1681	- What does a user give, and what claim do they receive in return?
1682	- What is that claim worth, and which variables determine the value?
1683	- Where does yield come from, and who is entitled to it?
1684	- What happens when the protocol is short — who absorbs the shortfall?
1685	
1686	If you cannot answer these without Solidity jargon, you are not ready to find his class of bug. Any spot where your plain-English explanation goes fuzzy is exactly where the bug is; mark it and come back.
1687	
1688	## Phase 1 — Build the money map
1689	
1690	For every storage variable that claims to be an aggregate — `total*`, `*Supply`, `*Balance`, `*Deposited`, `*Locked`, `*Reserve`, `*Debt`, `*Accrued`, indices, cumulative rates — enumerate **every** function that writes it and whether that write increases or decreases it.
1691	
1692	Then build the asymmetry table. Three columns of pure gold:
1693	
1694	| Asymmetry | What to look for | Real finding |
1695	| --- | --- | --- |
1696	| Moved without tracking | value transferred out with no matching decrement | *"Users redeeming early will withdraw `Ra` without decreasing the amount locked, which will lead to stolen funds when withdrawing after expiry"* |
1697	| Tracked in one branch only | `if` updates the total, `else` does not | *"Users will steal excess funds from the Vault due to `VaultPoolLib::redeem()` not always decreasing `raBalance` and `paBalance`"* |
1698	| Never tracked at all | a balance is real but no variable represents it | *"Total `ETH`, `WETH` and `gameETH` are not tracked which will lead to insolvency"* |
1699	
1700	Also flag every place a **live balance read** (`token.balanceOf(address(this))`, `address(this).balance`) is used as an accounting source. That is a donation attack or a cross-user theft waiting to happen — *"`ManagedLeveragedVault::openDen()` using all `asset()` balance"*, *"SDAIPriceFeed is vulnerable to donation attack via manipulatable vault rate"*.
1701	
1702	## Phase 2 — Write the invariants down
1703	
1704	5–15 statements that must always hold. Concretely, not vaguely:
1705	
1706	- `Σ(all user withdrawable) <= actual token balance` — the solvency invariant, his single most productive one
1707	- `totalX == Σ userX` for every aggregate with a per-user counterpart
1708	- every credited unit is debited exactly once, in exactly one place
1709	- monotonic things (indices, cumulative rates, timestamps) never go backwards and cannot be advanced for free
1710	- a user's claim cannot increase from an action that costs them nothing
1711	- state on chain A and chain B agree after every message settles
1712	
1713	An invariant you can state and then break with a sequence is a finding. An invariant the docs assert and the code does not enforce is his highest-yield source of all.
1714	
1715	## Phase 3 — Run the lifecycles, not the functions
1716	
1717	Do not audit function by function. Audit *sequences*, and after each step write down which accounting variables changed and which should have.
1718	
1719	Canonical sequences to run:
1720	
1721	1. deposit → accrue yield → withdraw
1722	2. deposit → borrow → price moves → liquidate → withdraw
1723	3. stake → rewards distributed → unstake → claim
1724	4. deposit → withdraw → deposit again (re-entry into the same accounting slot — *"Borrower deposit, withdraw, deposit will reinit `omniChainData.cdsPoolValue`"*)
1725	5. open → adjust position → close (does the adjust path keep every invariant the open path established? — *"The health of a `ProtectedListing` is incorrectly calculated if `tokenTaken` has been changed through `adjustPosition()`"*)
1726	6. source chain send → destination chain receive → failure/retry
1727	7. the same sequence at expiry / after maturity / after the vault has ended
1728	
1729	For each, ask at every step: **what did we just change that something else still assumes the old value of?**
1730	
1731	## Phase 4 — Attack across cohorts and across time
1732	
1733	This is the most distinctive part of his method, and the least commonly imitated.
1734	
1735	Value in DeFi is split pro-rata among a changing set of holders. Any calculation that uses a *current* total to distribute a *historically accumulated* amount lets someone join late and take a share of value they did not earn.
1736	
1737	Three questions, applied to every distribution, reward, fee, yield, and profit path:
1738	
1739	1. **Can I join immediately before a distribution and take a share of it?**
1740	   *"Immediately start getting rewards belonging to others after staking"*, *"Late abond holders steal USDa amount from liquidations from earlier abond holders"*, *"increaseNetworkTotal() allows big arbitrage opportunities by depositing before an increase transaction"*
1741	2. **Can I leave immediately before a loss and push it onto whoever stays?**
1742	   *"Borrower withdrawing at a loss will cause losses for cds depositors that only withdraw after the price recovers"*
1743	3. **The Last User Out test.** Have every user withdraw, in sequence, in the worst order. Does the last one get paid? If the protocol is short by even dust, the money map has a leak upstream — go find it.
1744	   *"`totalEarnings` is incorrect when withdrawing after ending which will withdraw too many funds leaving the `Vault` insolvent"*
1745	
1746	Cumulative-rate and index-based accounting deserves special hostility: check whether the index can be advanced without cost (*"Malicious user can call `calculateCumulativeRate()` any number of times to inflate debt rate as `lastEventTime` is not updated"*), and whether a user's snapshot is taken at the right moment (*"Depositing to another receiver other than `msg.sender` will lead to stuck funds by increasing `avgStart` without claiming"*).
1747	
1748	## Phase 5 — Saturate the subsystem
1749	
1750	When you find one bug, **do not move on**. His reports cluster: 38 findings in one protocol, most in a single accounting subsystem. That is not luck. Once the accounting model is in your head, mine it out.
1751	
1752	After every finding:
1753	1. Search the codebase for every other site with the same code shape — by function name *and* by pattern. If `redeem()` forgets a decrement, check `withdraw()`, `emergencyWithdraw()`, `redeemExpired()`, and the cross-chain variant.
1754	2. Attack the other branches of the function where you found it.
1755	3. Escalate: a DoS often conceals fund theft; a rounding error often compounds into drain. Push each finding to its worst exploitable variant before writing it up.
1756	
1757	A repeat instance you missed is an audit failure, not an omission.
1758	
1759	## Phase 6 — Prove it, with preconditions stated honestly
1760	
1761	His writeups make the reader's job trivial by separating what the protocol must look like from what the world must look like:
1762	
1763	- **Internal pre-conditions** — protocol state required (a maturity exists, a position is near liquidation, deposits are non-zero). "None" is common and is the strongest possible case.
1764	- **External pre-conditions** — market/oracle/chain conditions required (price moves X%, sequencer down, gas above Y). "None" is again the strongest case.
1765	- **Attack path** — numbered, concrete, with actors and numbers. Not "an attacker could manipulate the rate" but "1. User deposits 100e18. 2. User is liquidated via `liquidationType1()`, adding 5e18 USDa. 3. Attacker deposits via flashloan and withdraws, taking 4.9e18 of it."
1766	- **Impact** — who loses what. Name the victim class.
1767	
1768	If you cannot fill the attack path with real numbers, you have a LEAD. Say so. A well-described lead is worth more than a finding you inflated.
1769	
1770	## Phase 7 — Minimal mitigation
1771	
1772	One change, the smallest that removes the defect, stated in the protocol's own terms:
1773	
1774	- "Add a cumulative tracking variable to handle this case."
1775	- "Set the vesting interest to 0 when the new interest is 0."
1776	- "Decrease `raBalance` in the early-redemption branch as well."
1777	- "Use `mulDiv` when converting between token and share amounts."
1778	
1779	Not "refactor the accounting system." Not "consider adding validation." Name the operation to add, remove, or reorder.
1780	
1781	## Three habits that separate his findings from noise
1782	
1783	**Root cause is a missing operation at a named line.** Very often the bug is not a wrong line but an absent one. Write it that way: *"In `PsmLib.sol:125`, `self.psm.balances.ra.decLocked(amount)` is not called."* Pointing at the absence is what makes the fix obvious.
1784	
1785	**Judge what the code allows, never what the deployer intends.** "The admin wouldn't do that" is not a mitigation. But equally, "admin can rug" with no concrete mechanism is not a finding.
1786	
1787	**Doubt the clean-looking path hardest.** The functions that read as obviously correct are the ones everyone else also skipped. When a guard looks sufficient, name three specific ways to defeat it — with addresses, values, and states, not abstractions — before you accept it.
1788	
1789	## Do not report
1790	
1791	Admin-only functions doing admin things. Standard, accepted DeFi tradeoffs (ordinary MEV on a swap the user chose, rounding dust with no amplification, first-depositor inflation where `MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY` or a virtual-share offset is already present). Self-harm-only bugs. "Centralization risk" with no mechanism. Gas optimizations dressed as vulnerabilities. Missing zero-address checks on admin setters.
1792	# Lens 11 — Edge & Terminal States
1793	
1794	You own the states the developers never tested: empty, single, first, last, zero, maximum, expired, paused, ended, and cancelled.
1795	
1796	Code is written for the steady state — many users, non-zero balances, an ongoing period. Almost every function has at least one boundary where its assumptions quietly stop holding, and the terminal states (expiry, vault ended, program finished, last user) are where the accounting bugs concentrate because nobody re-derives the math for them.
1797	
1798	## The checklist — run every one against every stateful function
1799	
1800	**Zero / empty.** `totalSupply == 0`, no depositors, no stakers, zero rewards, zero amount, empty array. What does the division do? Where do distributed tokens go when there is nobody to receive them?
1801	> *Lost rewards when the supply is 0, which always happens if rewards are queued before anyone has StakeTracker tokens*
1802	> *Having no deposits in `StakedEXA` will lead to stuck rewards when harvesting*
1803	> *Utilization rates are 0 when average assets are 0, which may be used to game maturity borrows / deposits / withdrawals*
1804	> *Unconditional lastUpdated advance in RangePool.sync leads to loss of streamed BMX when pool liquidity == 0*
1805	
1806	**One / sole occupant.** A single participant, one wei, one share, the only LP. Strict `<` guards frequently exclude the legitimate sole-occupant case; verify `<=` is the right comparator on every count check.
1807	> *A malicious user may unlock instantly all the funds from the `FluidLocker` when no one is staking in the Tax pool*
1808	> *`ClearingHouseLiq::_finalizeSubaccount()` does not check if the subaccount has lps*
1809	> *Unassigned pool earnings can be stolen when a maturity borrow is liquidated by depositing at maturity with 1 principal*
1810	
1811	**First.** First depositor, first mint, pool creation, initialization. Who sets the initial rate and can it be set adversarially?
1812	> *`BoldToken` initialization can be frontrun to silently mint/approve bold to an attacker*
1813	> *Incorrect initial deposit calculation may cause cancelProgram to revert*
1814	
1815	**Last.** The last withdrawer, the last share burned, the final unit of supply, the last bond. This is his highest-yield edge: run the full unwind and check whether the final actor is paid and whether residual value is trapped.
1816	> *User to sell the last supply will make the exchange contribution forever stuck*
1817	> *Interest generated by last bond will not go to anyone when liquidating as there is no bond amount to collect it*
1818	> *`totalEarnings` is incorrect when withdrawing after ending which will withdraw too many funds leaving the `Vault` insolvent*
1819	> *Liquidator will leave a pool with unassigned earnings on `Market::clearBadDebt()` free to claim for anyone when the repaid maturity is not the last*
1820	
1821	**Expired / matured / ended.** Every function behaves differently after expiry, and the expiry-path variants are the least reviewed code in any protocol. Re-run the whole lifecycle past the boundary.
1822	> *Users redeeming early will withdraw `Ra` without decreasing the amount locked, which will lead to stolen funds when withdrawing after expiry*
1823	> *Withdrawing all `lv` before expiry will lead to lost funds in the Vault*

1540	### DESIGN.md (in-scope clean specification)
1541	
1542	```markdown
1543	# Clean design specification
1544	Ethereum NFT raffle; immutable factory, ERC-1167 clones with immutable implementation. One entry costs 1,000,000 units of canonical six-decimal USDC. One purchase mints a transferable ERC721 ticket representing a contiguous inclusive range. Exactly one ERC721 prize is escrowed atomically at creation. Reserve met awards NFT and 95% sponsor / 5% treasury. Reserve missed awards 80% gross to winner, 15% sponsor, 5% treasury. Refund outcome pays 100% per entry and returns prize. Rounding is floor on aggregate protocol fee; remainder must be allocated without loss. No administrator, mutable configuration or upgrade. Request window [sale end, end+2days); callback accepted strictly before request timestamp+2days. Refunds open at deadline. Callback records result only. Settlement is permissionless, storage-only; redemption requires current ticket owner, burns claim atomically, and must revert all effects on delivery failure. Sponsor and treasury can claim independently after settlement. Never move assets between raffle clones. Quote token and Chainlink wrapper are trusted canonical dependencies; arbitrary prize contracts and ticket recipients are untrusted. Frontend discovery is advisory; transaction decisions must reread current chain state.
1545	
1546	This specification was composed before scanner results and historical findings. Source, not design prose, determines actual behavior. No tests, audit history, accepted-risk lists or scanner results are provided.
1547	```

1549	# Money Map — raffle.fun (Raffle clone + RaffleFactory)
1550	
1551	Built by the orchestrator from `DESIGN.md` (clean spec) plus source. Line numbers are `Raffle.sol` unless prefixed `F:` (`RaffleFactory.sol`) or `I:` (`IRaffle.sol`).

1647	# The 0xSimao Method
1648	
1649	Derived from 869 published findings across 143 reviews. This is HOW to think. Your lens file is WHAT to look for. Work them together.
1650	
1651	## The core thesis
1652	
1653	Most auditors read code looking for bad lines. That finds the bugs a linter finds.
1654	
1655	0xSimao reads code looking for **a claim that has drifted from what actually backs it**. Value moves through a protocol in sequences: deposit, accrue, borrow, liquidate, withdraw. Each step writes some subset of the accounting state, and drift is any way that state stops describing reality:
1656	
1657	| Drift | Shape |
1658	| --- | --- |
1659	| The write is missing | value moved and no variable recorded it — or one branch updates it and the sibling branch does not |
1660	| The write is wrong | the variable is updated with the wrong amount, direction, rounding, units, or decimals |
1661	| The write is mistimed | the right value at the wrong moment, so someone's snapshot is taken against state that is about to change |
1662	| The write goes to the wrong party | the total is intact; the split between cohorts is not |
1663	| The input was never trustworthy | the number is faithfully propagated from an oracle, a live balance, or a caller-supplied parameter an attacker controls |
1664	| The state is unreachable | the accounting is correct but a revert, a pause, an unbounded loop, or a missing path means it can never be settled |
1665	
1666	The drift is invisible at any single line. It only appears when you ask: *after this whole sequence, does the protocol still owe exactly what it holds — and can everyone actually collect it?*
1667	
1668	A defect nobody can be shown to lose money from is a curiosity. So every candidate gets one more question, and it is the one that separates a finding from a smell:
1669	
1670	> **Who is left holding the loss?**
1671	
1672	Answer with a named class of actor, never "users". For accounting drift it is often whoever withdraws last, because a shortfall stays invisible until the balance runs out — but for a bricked liquidation it is the solvent lenders eating the bad debt, for a mistimed snapshot it is the cohort that held through the accrual, and for a forged signature it is whoever the forged message was drawn against. If the only person worse off is the caller, there is no finding.
1673	
1674	**This lens is the sharpest one, not the only one.** Accounting drift is the largest single class in his corpus, but it is not the majority of it. The rest is DoS and permanently stuck funds, access control and signature defects, token- and integration-behaviour assumptions (`USDT` approvals, fee-on-transfer, blacklists, pausable collateral), oracle and parameter validation, and cross-chain state — and those are what your lens file owns. Work the money map first because it is what makes the drift class visible; then work your lens on its own terms. When the target has little accounting to speak of — a router, a registry, a verifier, a signature scheme — say so, keep the money map short, and go straight to your lens. Do not force a finding into the drift frame to make it sound like his.
1675	
1676	## Phase 0 — Learn the protocol's own vocabulary before reading for bugs
1677	
1678	His findings are written in the protocol's language: `cdsPoolValue`, `abond`, `downsideProtected`, `unassignedEarnings`, `raBalance`, `floatingBackupBorrowed`. He does not audit "a vault"; he audits *this* vault's specific accounting model.
1679	
1680	Before hunting, be able to state in plain English:
1681	- What does a user give, and what claim do they receive in return?
1682	- What is that claim worth, and which variables determine the value?
1683	- Where does yield come from, and who is entitled to it?
1684	- What happens when the protocol is short — who absorbs the shortfall?
1685	
1686	If you cannot answer these without Solidity jargon, you are not ready to find his class of bug. Any spot where your plain-English explanation goes fuzzy is exactly where the bug is; mark it and come back.
1687	
1688	## Phase 1 — Build the money map
1689	
1690	For every storage variable that claims to be an aggregate — `total*`, `*Supply`, `*Balance`, `*Deposited`, `*Locked`, `*Reserve`, `*Debt`, `*Accrued`, indices, cumulative rates — enumerate **every** function that writes it and whether that write increases or decreases it.
1691	
1692	Then build the asymmetry table. Three columns of pure gold:
1693	
1694	| Asymmetry | What to look for | Real finding |
1695	| --- | --- | --- |
1696	| Moved without tracking | value transferred out with no matching decrement | *"Users redeeming early will withdraw `Ra` without decreasing the amount locked, which will lead to stolen funds when withdrawing after expiry"* |
1697	| Tracked in one branch only | `if` updates the total, `else` does not | *"Users will steal excess funds from the Vault due to `VaultPoolLib::redeem()` not always decreasing `raBalance` and `paBalance`"* |
1698	| Never tracked at all | a balance is real but no variable represents it | *"Total `ETH`, `WETH` and `gameETH` are not tracked which will lead to insolvency"* |
1699	
1700	Also flag every place a **live balance read** (`token.balanceOf(address(this))`, `address(this).balance`) is used as an accounting source. That is a donation attack or a cross-user theft waiting to happen — *"`ManagedLeveragedVault::openDen()` using all `asset()` balance"*, *"SDAIPriceFeed is vulnerable to donation attack via manipulatable vault rate"*.
1701	
1702	## Phase 2 — Write the invariants down
1703	
1704	5–15 statements that must always hold. Concretely, not vaguely:
1705	
1706	- `Σ(all user withdrawable) <= actual token balance` — the solvency invariant, his single most productive one
1707	- `totalX == Σ userX` for every aggregate with a per-user counterpart
1708	- every credited unit is debited exactly once, in exactly one place
1709	- monotonic things (indices, cumulative rates, timestamps) never go backwards and cannot be advanced for free
1710	- a user's claim cannot increase from an action that costs them nothing
1711	- state on chain A and chain B agree after every message settles
1712	
1713	An invariant you can state and then break with a sequence is a finding. An invariant the docs assert and the code does not enforce is his highest-yield source of all.
1714	
1715	## Phase 3 — Run the lifecycles, not the functions
1716	
1717	Do not audit function by function. Audit *sequences*, and after each step write down which accounting variables changed and which should have.
1718	
1719	Canonical sequences to run:
1720	
1721	1. deposit → accrue yield → withdraw
1722	2. deposit → borrow → price moves → liquidate → withdraw
1723	3. stake → rewards distributed → unstake → claim
1724	4. deposit → withdraw → deposit again (re-entry into the same accounting slot — *"Borrower deposit, withdraw, deposit will reinit `omniChainData.cdsPoolValue`"*)
1725	5. open → adjust position → close (does the adjust path keep every invariant the open path established? — *"The health of a `ProtectedListing` is incorrectly calculated if `tokenTaken` has been changed through `adjustPosition()`"*)
1726	6. source chain send → destination chain receive → failure/retry
1727	7. the same sequence at expiry / after maturity / after the vault has ended
1728	
1729	For each, ask at every step: **what did we just change that something else still assumes the old value of?**
1730	
1731	## Phase 4 — Attack across cohorts and across time
1732	
1733	This is the most distinctive part of his method, and the least commonly imitated.
1734	
1735	Value in DeFi is split pro-rata among a changing set of holders. Any calculation that uses a *current* total to distribute a *historically accumulated* amount lets someone join late and take a share of value they did not earn.
1736	
1737	Three questions, applied to every distribution, reward, fee, yield, and profit path:
1738	
1739	1. **Can I join immediately before a distribution and take a share of it?**
1740	   *"Immediately start getting rewards belonging to others after staking"*, *"Late abond holders steal USDa amount from liquidations from earlier abond holders"*, *"increaseNetworkTotal() allows big arbitrage opportunities by depositing before an increase transaction"*
1741	2. **Can I leave immediately before a loss and push it onto whoever stays?**
1742	   *"Borrower withdrawing at a loss will cause losses for cds depositors that only withdraw after the price recovers"*
1743	3. **The Last User Out test.** Have every user withdraw, in sequence, in the worst order. Does the last one get paid? If the protocol is short by even dust, the money map has a leak upstream — go find it.
1744	   *"`totalEarnings` is incorrect when withdrawing after ending which will withdraw too many funds leaving the `Vault` insolvent"*
1745	
1746	Cumulative-rate and index-based accounting deserves special hostility: check whether the index can be advanced without cost (*"Malicious user can call `calculateCumulativeRate()` any number of times to inflate debt rate as `lastEventTime` is not updated"*), and whether a user's snapshot is taken at the right moment (*"Depositing to another receiver other than `msg.sender` will lead to stuck funds by increasing `avgStart` without claiming"*).
1747	
1748	## Phase 5 — Saturate the subsystem
1749	
1750	When you find one bug, **do not move on**. His reports cluster: 38 findings in one protocol, most in a single accounting subsystem. That is not luck. Once the accounting model is in your head, mine it out.
1751	
1752	After every finding:
1753	1. Search the codebase for every other site with the same code shape — by function name *and* by pattern. If `redeem()` forgets a decrement, check `withdraw()`, `emergencyWithdraw()`, `redeemExpired()`, and the cross-chain variant.
1754	2. Attack the other branches of the function where you found it.
1755	3. Escalate: a DoS often conceals fund theft; a rounding error often compounds into drain. Push each finding to its worst exploitable variant before writing it up.
1756	
1757	A repeat instance you missed is an audit failure, not an omission.
1758	
1759	## Phase 6 — Prove it, with preconditions stated honestly
1760	
1761	His writeups make the reader's job trivial by separating what the protocol must look like from what the world must look like:
1762	
1763	- **Internal pre-conditions** — protocol state required (a maturity exists, a position is near liquidation, deposits are non-zero). "None" is common and is the strongest possible case.
1764	- **External pre-conditions** — market/oracle/chain conditions required (price moves X%, sequencer down, gas above Y). "None" is again the strongest case.
1765	- **Attack path** — numbered, concrete, with actors and numbers. Not "an attacker could manipulate the rate" but "1. User deposits 100e18. 2. User is liquidated via `liquidationType1()`, adding 5e18 USDa. 3. Attacker deposits via flashloan and withdraws, taking 4.9e18 of it."
1766	- **Impact** — who loses what. Name the victim class.
1767	
1768	If you cannot fill the attack path with real numbers, you have a LEAD. Say so. A well-described lead is worth more than a finding you inflated.
1769	
1770	## Phase 7 — Minimal mitigation
1771	
1772	One change, the smallest that removes the defect, stated in the protocol's own terms:
1773	
1774	- "Add a cumulative tracking variable to handle this case."
1775	- "Set the vesting interest to 0 when the new interest is 0."
1776	- "Decrease `raBalance` in the early-redemption branch as well."
1777	- "Use `mulDiv` when converting between token and share amounts."
1778	
1779	Not "refactor the accounting system." Not "consider adding validation." Name the operation to add, remove, or reorder.
1780	
1781	## Three habits that separate his findings from noise
1782	
1783	**Root cause is a missing operation at a named line.** Very often the bug is not a wrong line but an absent one. Write it that way: *"In `PsmLib.sol:125`, `self.psm.balances.ra.decLocked(amount)` is not called."* Pointing at the absence is what makes the fix obvious.
1784	
1785	**Judge what the code allows, never what the deployer intends.** "The admin wouldn't do that" is not a mitigation. But equally, "admin can rug" with no concrete mechanism is not a finding.
1786	
1787	**Doubt the clean-looking path hardest.** The functions that read as obviously correct are the ones everyone else also skipped. When a guard looks sufficient, name three specific ways to defeat it — with addresses, values, and states, not abstractions — before you accept it.
1788	
1789	## Do not report
1790	
1791	Admin-only functions doing admin things. Standard, accepted DeFi tradeoffs (ordinary MEV on a swap the user chose, rounding dust with no amplification, first-depositor inflation where `MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY` or a virtual-share offset is already present). Self-harm-only bugs. "Centralization risk" with no mechanism. Gas optimizations dressed as vulnerabilities. Missing zero-address checks on admin setters.
1792	# Lens 12 — Flow Completeness & Symmetry
1793	
1794	You are the gap hunter. Every other lens looks for wrong code; you look for **absent code** — the call that should be there and is not, the branch that handles one case and not its mirror, the path that exists in one function and is missing from its sibling.
1795	
1796	This is where 0xSimao's root causes most often land. His phrasing is usually literally *"X is not called"*, *"Y is not updated"*, *"Z is not taken into account"*. You cannot grep for a missing line; you find it by demanding symmetry.
1797	
1798	## The four symmetries
1799	
1800	**1. Inverse symmetry — every forward operation needs its exact inverse.**
1801	
1802	Pair them up and diff the two implementations line by line: deposit/withdraw, mint/burn, stake/unstake, lock/unlock, open/close, borrow/repay, add/remove, schedule/cancel, send/receive. Whatever the forward path writes, the inverse must unwrite. List the forward's state writes in one column and the inverse's in the other; every unmatched row is a candidate.
1803	
1804	> *Staked tokens inside FluidLocker can be withdrawn without calling Unstake*
1805	> *Method refundPlayers doesn't update `_lockedETH` in WinnableTicketManager*
1806	> *Pumponomics can be skipped when using `FluidLocker::provideLiquidity`*
1807	
1808	**2. Sibling symmetry — functions in the same family must handle the same cases.**
1809	
1810	If a protocol has `withdraw`, `redeem`, `emergencyWithdraw`, `redeemExpired`, and a cross-chain variant, they all touch the same accounting. Take the most complete one as the reference and diff every sibling against it. The forgotten one is never the main path — it is the expiry variant, the emergency variant, or the one added last.
1811	
1812	> *Users will steal excess funds from the Vault due to `VaultPoolLib::redeem()` not always decreasing `raBalance` and `paBalance`*
1813	> *`CDSLib::withdrawUserWhoNotOptedForLiq()` tax is not stored in the treasury*
1814	> *Inconsistent Use of `lastCumulativeRate` in `depositTokens()` and `withdraw()` Functions*
1815	> *`BlueBundlesV1::blueBundlesV1RepayAndWithdrawCollateral()` may transfer a null leftover* (the sibling above it skips when null)
1816	
1817	**3. Branch symmetry — both arms of every conditional must leave state consistent.**
1818	
1819	For every `if`/`else`, `try`/`catch`, early `return`, and `require` that skips work: list the state each arm writes. Unequal sets are the finding. Same for loops with `continue`.
1820	
1821	> *`CDSLib::calculateCumulativeRate()` incorrectly only increments the local option fees when there are cds deposits*
1822	> *Protected downside is not updated when `cds.getTotalCdsDepositedAmount() < downsideProtected`*
1823	> *`TradingLimits::update()` incorrectly only rounds up when `deltaFlowUnits` becomes 0*
1824	
1825	**4. Precondition symmetry — every function that consumes derived state must first refresh it.**
1826	
1827	Accrual, sync, checkpoint, settle, harvest, and update calls form a discipline: some functions call them and some forget. Find every reader of a time-dependent or index-dependent value and confirm the refresh happens first. Then check the refresh itself updates its own `lastUpdated`.
1828	
1829	> *Market interest is not always accrued*
1830	> *Profitable liquidations and accumulation of bad debt due to earnings accumulator not being triggered before liquidating*
1831	> *`ManagedLeveragedVault::executeWithdrawalEpoch()` will never work because `cd.prevICR` is not set*
1832	> *Malicious user can call `borrowing::calculateCumulativeRate()` any number of times to inflate debt rate as `lastEventTime` is not updated*
1833	
1834	## Additional gap patterns
1835	
1836	**Wrong-thing-validated.** A check exists and looks reassuring, but validates a different field than the one that matters. These survive review precisely because a check is present.
1837	> *`UniswapLiquidityAssetManager::_validateCollectFeesArgs()` validates nullifier instead of note footer*
1838	> *WBTCZapper approves wrong token for exchange*
1839	
1840	**Return value discarded.** The callee reports what actually happened; the caller assumes what it requested.
1841	> *Providing liquidity to the AMM does not check the return value of actually provided tokens leading to locked funds*
1842	> *`FlashSwapRouter::emptyReserve()` and `emptyReservePartial()` functions return incorrect values*
1843	
1844	**Missing initialization.** An `__X_init()` never called, a field never set, a hardcoded index where a computed one belongs.
1845	> *Missing `__Ownable_init()` call in `LenderCommitmentGroup_Smart::initialize()`*
1846	> *`createCommonProjectIDAndDeploymentRequest()` hardcodes request id index to 0, leading to lost requests for users*
1847	
1848	**Documented-but-absent.** Read the docs, README, NatSpec, and comments as a specification, then verify each claim in code. A behavior the docs promise and the code does not implement is a finding, and it is the easiest kind to argue.
1849	> *Rebasing tokens are not supported contrary to the readme and will lead to loss of funds*
1850	> *Withdrawals and Claims are meant to be pausable, but it is not possible in practice*
1851	> *Rank and multiplier of a user can not be set if the user is registered for `MetaIDO` by the admin*
1852	
1853	**Copy-paste divergence.** Near-identical blocks where one was updated and the other was not. Diff them character by character.
1854	> *Code has typos in `RebalanceLogic::repayAavePosition()` leading to undefined behaviour*
1855	
1856	## Method
1857	
1858	Work from tables, not intuition. Build the forward/inverse table, the sibling table, and the branch table for every family in the money map. The gaps are visible in the tables and invisible in the code.
1859	
1860	## Every finding needs the missing operation named
1861	
1862	State it as an absence at a specific line: *"In `PsmLib.sol:125`, `self.psm.balances.ra.decLocked(amount)` is not called, unlike in `redeemWithCt()` at line 88."* Point at what is absent and cite the sibling that has it. That framing makes the mitigation self-evident.
1863	# Shared Lens Rules
1864	
1865	## Bundle contents
1866	
1867	Your bundle is five concatenated parts: all in-scope source, the protocol's **money map** (built by the orchestrator), the **method** (how to think), your **lens** (what you own), and these shared rules (output format and protocol).
1868	
1869	Read the whole bundle once at the start. Do not re-read in-scope files for the initial scan. Read or search the repo only for cross-file lookups or out-of-scope context (`interfaces/`, `lib/`, `mocks/`, `test/`).
1870	
1871	**Start from the money map, not the file list.** Pick the tracked totals, lifecycles, and cohorts your lens owns, and attack those. The file list is where you go to confirm, not where you begin.
1872	
1873	When matching function names, check both `functionName` and `_functionName` (Solidity convention), and check library variants (`XLib::function`).
1874	
1875	## Public audit-evidence summaries
1876	
1877	Provide concise public audit evidence and final conclusions, with source references. Do not provide private working text, hidden chain-of-thought, or a transcript of internal deliberation. The following labels organize the public report; they are not instructions to reveal private reasoning or to emit intermediate working text before continuing.
1878	
1879	| Evidence category | Public label | Brief report content |
1880	| --- | --- | --- |
1881	| A function moves value or writes a tracked total | `[Model: <name>]` | Summarize what a user gives, what they receive, and the totals changed, citing the relevant function. |
1882	| A non-obvious operation relies on an assumption | `[Why: <file:line>]` | State the relevant assumption and the source evidence establishing it, or identify the unresolved assumption. |
1883	| An access guard or value-moving path is assessed | `[Defeat: <function>]` | Report concise boundary-test or adversarial-case outcomes and the effective guard or uncovered condition; no private deliberation is requested. |
1884	| A lifecycle is assessed | `[LastOut: <lifecycle>]` | State the conservation/liability result and whether all eligible users can receive the amounts owed, with evidence or a clearly identified gap. |
1885	
1886	Use these summaries as public evidence for the audit result. The orchestrator may inventory which evidence categories were covered; it must not request or evaluate private reasoning traces. All remaining lens scope, saturation, finding format, severity, adjudication, proof and reporting rules are unchanged.
1887	
1888	## Saturation is mandatory
1889	
1890	When you find a bug, weaponize the pattern across the entire codebase before moving on. Search by function name AND by code shape. If one redemption path forgets a decrement, check every other redemption, withdrawal, emergency, expiry, and cross-chain variant. Then attack the other branches of the function where you found it. Then escalate the finding to its worst exploitable variant — a DoS often hides fund theft.
1891	
1892	A repeat instance you missed is an audit failure.
1893	
1894	## Do not report
1895	
1896	Admin-only functions doing admin things. Accepted DeFi tradeoffs (ordinary MEV on a user-chosen swap, rounding dust with no amplification path, first-depositor inflation where a virtual-share offset or `MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY` already exists). Self-harm-only bugs. "Centralization risk" or "admin can rug" without a concrete mechanism. Missing zero-address checks on admin setters. Gas findings.
1897	
1898	## Output
1899	
1900	FINDINGs have a concrete, unguarded, exploitable path with a named victim. LEADs have a real accounting or logic smell with a partial path. Default to LEAD over dropping — never drop.
1901	
1902	**One vulnerability per block.** Same root cause = one block. Needs a different fix = separate block.
1903	
1904	```
1905	FINDING | contract: Name | function: func | bug_class: kebab-tag | group_key: Contract | function | bug-class
1906	root_cause: the defect at File.sol:LINE, naming the missing or wrong operation
1907	internal_pre: protocol state required, or None
1908	external_pre: market/oracle/chain conditions required, or None
1909	path:
1910	  1. actor does X with concrete amount
1911	  2. state changes to Y
1912	  3. actor does Z
1913	impact: who loses what, and who is left holding the loss
1914	mitigation: the single smallest change that removes the defect
1915	```
1916	
1917	```
1918	LEAD | contract: Name | function: func | bug_class: kebab-tag | group_key: Contract | function | bug-class
1919	smell: what you found
1920	unverified: precisely what you could not establish
1921	description: one sentence on the trail
1922	```
1923	
1924	`group_key` drives deduplication and is always `ContractName | functionName | bug_class`.
1925	
1926	An `internal_pre` or `external_pre` of `None` is the strongest possible finding — never pad these to look thorough. State the truth.

"""Mechanical extractor for Turn 6 (dedup + completeness gate).

Reads raw lens outputs (lens-N-output.md), finds every FINDING / LEAD header line in the
shared-rules format, and emits a JSON inventory plus the unique (Contract, function) set.
It parses text only; it makes no security judgement.

Usage: python3 -I extract_items.py <raw_dir> <out_json>
"""
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HEADER = re.compile(
    r"^\s*[`*>\-]*\s*(?P<kind>FINDING|LEAD)\s*\|\s*contract:\s*(?P<contract>[^|]+?)\s*\|\s*"
    r"function:\s*(?P<function>[^|]+?)\s*\|\s*bug_class:\s*(?P<bug_class>[^|]+?)\s*\|\s*"
    r"group_key:\s*(?P<group_key>.+?)\s*[`*]*\s*$"
)
FIELD = re.compile(r"^\s*(root_cause|internal_pre|external_pre|impact|mitigation|smell|unverified|description):\s*(.*)$")


def parse(path: Path):
    lens = re.search(r"lens-(\d+)-output", path.name)
    lens_no = int(lens.group(1)) if lens else None
    items = []
    current = None
    for lineno, line in enumerate(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), 1):
        m = HEADER.match(line)
        if m:
            current = {k: v.strip() for k, v in m.groupdict().items()}
            current.update({"lens": lens_no, "line": lineno, "fields": {}})
            items.append(current)
            continue
        if current is not None:
            f = FIELD.match(line)
            if f and f.group(1) not in current["fields"]:
                current["fields"][f.group(1)] = f.group(2).strip()
    return items


def main():
    raw_dir, out_json = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2])
    files = sorted(raw_dir.glob("lens-*-output.md"), key=lambda p: int(re.search(r"lens-(\d+)", p.name).group(1)))
    inventory = []
    for p in files:
        inventory.extend(parse(p))
    pairs = sorted({(i["contract"], i["function"]) for i in inventory})
    summary = {
        "files": [p.name for p in files],
        "counts": {
            "FINDING": sum(1 for i in inventory if i["kind"] == "FINDING"),
            "LEAD": sum(1 for i in inventory if i["kind"] == "LEAD"),
            "per_lens": {str(n): sum(1 for i in inventory if i["lens"] == n) for n in sorted({i["lens"] for i in inventory})},
        },
        "unique_contract_function": [list(p) for p in pairs],
        "items": inventory,
    }
    out_json.write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"files={len(files)} FINDING={summary['counts']['FINDING']} LEAD={summary['counts']['LEAD']} unique(C,f)={len(pairs)}")
    for i in inventory:
        print(f"L{i['lens']:>2} {i['kind']:<7} {i['contract']} | {i['function']} | {i['bug_class']}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

1	// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
     2	pragma solidity ^0.8.0;
     3	
     4	import {LinkTokenInterface} from "../../shared/interfaces/LinkTokenInterface.sol";
     5	import {IVRFV2PlusWrapper} from "./interfaces/IVRFV2PlusWrapper.sol";
     6	
     7	/**
     8	 *
     9	 * @notice Interface for contracts using VRF randomness through the VRF V2 wrapper
    10	 * ********************************************************************************
    11	 * @dev PURPOSE
    12	 *
    13	 * @dev Create VRF V2+ requests without the need for subscription management. Rather than creating
    14	 * @dev and funding a VRF V2+ subscription, a user can use this wrapper to create one off requests,
    15	 * @dev paying up front rather than at fulfillment.
    16	 *
    17	 * @dev Since the price is determined using the gas price of the request transaction rather than
    18	 * @dev the fulfillment transaction, the wrapper charges an additional premium on callback gas
    19	 * @dev usage, in addition to some extra overhead costs associated with the VRFV2Wrapper contract.
    20	 * *****************************************************************************
    21	 * @dev USAGE
    22	 *
    23	 * @dev Calling contracts must inherit from VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase. The consumer must be funded
    24	 * @dev with enough LINK or ether to make the request, otherwise requests will revert. To request randomness,
    25	 * @dev call the 'requestRandomWords' function with the desired VRF parameters. This function handles
    26	 * @dev paying for the request based on the current pricing.
    27	 *
    28	 * @dev Consumers must implement the fullfillRandomWords function, which will be called during
    29	 * @dev fulfillment with the randomness result.
    30	 */
    31	abstract contract VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase {
    32	  error OnlyVRFWrapperCanFulfill(address have, address want);
    33	
    34	  LinkTokenInterface internal immutable i_linkToken;
    35	  IVRFV2PlusWrapper public immutable i_vrfV2PlusWrapper;
    36	
    37	  /**
    38	   * @param _vrfV2PlusWrapper is the address of the VRFV2Wrapper contract
    39	   */
    40	  constructor(
    41	    address _vrfV2PlusWrapper
    42	  ) {
    43	    IVRFV2PlusWrapper vrfV2PlusWrapper = IVRFV2PlusWrapper(_vrfV2PlusWrapper);
    44	
    45	    i_linkToken = LinkTokenInterface(vrfV2PlusWrapper.link());
    46	    i_vrfV2PlusWrapper = vrfV2PlusWrapper;
    47	  }
    48	
    49	  /**
    50	   * @dev Requests randomness from the VRF V2+ wrapper.
    51	   *
    52	   * @param _callbackGasLimit is the gas limit that should be used when calling the consumer's
    53	   *        fulfillRandomWords function.
    54	   * @param _requestConfirmations is the number of confirmations to wait before fulfilling the
    55	   *        request. A higher number of confirmations increases security by reducing the likelihood
    56	   *        that a chain re-org changes a published randomness outcome.
    57	   * @param _numWords is the number of random words to request.
    58	   *
    59	   * @return requestId is the VRF V2+ request ID of the newly created randomness request.
    60	   */
    61	  // solhint-disable-next-line chainlink-solidity/prefix-internal-functions-with-underscore
    62	  function requestRandomness(
    63	    uint32 _callbackGasLimit,
    64	    uint16 _requestConfirmations,
    65	    uint32 _numWords,
    66	    bytes memory extraArgs
    67	  ) internal returns (uint256 requestId, uint256 reqPrice) {
    68	    reqPrice = i_vrfV2PlusWrapper.calculateRequestPrice(_callbackGasLimit, _numWords);
    69	    i_linkToken.transferAndCall(
    70	      address(i_vrfV2PlusWrapper), reqPrice, abi.encode(_callbackGasLimit, _requestConfirmations, _numWords, extraArgs)
    71	    );
    72	    return (i_vrfV2PlusWrapper.lastRequestId(), reqPrice);
    73	  }
    74	
    75	  // solhint-disable-next-line chainlink-solidity/prefix-internal-functions-with-underscore
    76	  function requestRandomnessPayInNative(
    77	    uint32 _callbackGasLimit,
    78	    uint16 _requestConfirmations,
    79	    uint32 _numWords,
    80	    bytes memory extraArgs
    81	  ) internal returns (uint256 requestId, uint256 requestPrice) {
    82	    requestPrice = i_vrfV2PlusWrapper.calculateRequestPriceNative(_callbackGasLimit, _numWords);
    83	    return (
    84	      i_vrfV2PlusWrapper.requestRandomWordsInNative{value: requestPrice}(
    85	        _callbackGasLimit, _requestConfirmations, _numWords, extraArgs
    86	      ),
    87	      requestPrice
    88	    );
    89	  }
    90	
    91	  /**
    92	   * @notice fulfillRandomWords handles the VRF V2 wrapper response. The consuming contract must
    93	   * @notice implement it.
    94	   *
    95	   * @param _requestId is the VRF V2 request ID.
    96	   * @param _randomWords is the randomness result.
    97	   */
    98	  // solhint-disable-next-line chainlink-solidity/prefix-internal-functions-with-underscore
    99	  function fulfillRandomWords(uint256 _requestId, uint256[] memory _randomWords) internal virtual;
   100	
   101	  function rawFulfillRandomWords(uint256 _requestId, uint256[] memory _randomWords) external {
   102	    address vrfWrapperAddr = address(i_vrfV2PlusWrapper);
   103	    if (msg.sender != vrfWrapperAddr) {
   104	      revert OnlyVRFWrapperCanFulfill(msg.sender, vrfWrapperAddr);
   105	    }
   106	    fulfillRandomWords(_requestId, _randomWords);
   107	  }
   108	
   109	  /// @notice getBalance returns the native balance of the consumer contract
   110	  function getBalance() public view returns (uint256) {
   111	    return address(this).balance;
   112	  }
   113	
   114	  /// @notice getLinkToken returns the link token contract
   115	  function getLinkToken() public view returns (LinkTokenInterface) {
   116	    return i_linkToken;
   117	  }
   118	}

     2	pragma solidity ^0.8.0;
     3	
     4	interface IVRFV2PlusWrapper {
     5	  /**
     6	   * @return the request ID of the most recent VRF V2 request made by this wrapper. This should only
     7	   * be relied option within the same transaction that the request was made.
     8	   */
     9	  function lastRequestId() external view returns (uint256);
    10	
    11	  /**
    12	   * @notice Calculates the price of a VRF request with the given callbackGasLimit at the current
    13	   * @notice block.
    14	   *
    15	   * @dev This function relies on the transaction gas price which is not automatically set during
    16	   * @dev simulation. To estimate the price at a specific gas price, use the estimatePrice function.
    17	   *
    18	   * @param _callbackGasLimit is the gas limit used to estimate the price.
    19	   * @param _numWords is the number of words to request.
    20	   */
    21	  function calculateRequestPrice(uint32 _callbackGasLimit, uint32 _numWords) external view returns (uint256);
    22	
    23	  /**
    24	   * @notice Calculates the price of a VRF request in native with the given callbackGasLimit at the current
    25	   * @notice block.
    26	   *
    27	   * @dev This function relies on the transaction gas price which is not automatically set during
    28	   * @dev simulation. To estimate the price at a specific gas price, use the estimatePrice function.
    29	   *
    30	   * @param _callbackGasLimit is the gas limit used to estimate the price.
    31	   * @param _numWords is the number of words to request.
    32	   */
    33	  function calculateRequestPriceNative(uint32 _callbackGasLimit, uint32 _numWords) external view returns (uint256);
    34	
    35	  /**
    36	   * @notice Estimates the price of a VRF request with a specific gas limit and gas price.
    37	   *
    38	   * @dev This is a convenience function that can be called in simulation to better understand
    39	   * @dev pricing.
    40	   *
    41	   * @param _callbackGasLimit is the gas limit used to estimate the price.
    42	   * @param _numWords is the number of words to request.
    43	   * @param _requestGasPriceWei is the gas price in wei used for the estimation.
    44	   */
    45	  function estimateRequestPrice(
    46	    uint32 _callbackGasLimit,
    47	    uint32 _numWords,
    48	    uint256 _requestGasPriceWei
    49	  ) external view returns (uint256);
    50	
    51	  /**
    52	   * @notice Estimates the price of a VRF request in native with a specific gas limit and gas price.
    53	   *
    54	   * @dev This is a convenience function that can be called in simulation to better understand
    55	   * @dev pricing.
    56	   *
    57	   * @param _callbackGasLimit is the gas limit used to estimate the price.
    58	   * @param _numWords is the number of words to request.
    59	   * @param _requestGasPriceWei is the gas price in wei used for the estimation.
    60	   */
    61	  function estimateRequestPriceNative(
    62	    uint32 _callbackGasLimit,
    63	    uint32 _numWords,
    64	    uint256 _requestGasPriceWei
    65	  ) external view returns (uint256);
    66	
    67	  /**
    68	   * @notice Requests randomness from the VRF V2 wrapper, paying in native token.
    69	   *
    70	   * @param _callbackGasLimit is the gas limit for the request.
    71	   * @param _requestConfirmations number of request confirmations to wait before serving a request.
    72	   * @param _numWords is the number of words to request.
    73	   */
    74	  function requestRandomWordsInNative(
    75	    uint32 _callbackGasLimit,
    76	    uint16 _requestConfirmations,
    77	    uint32 _numWords,
    78	    bytes calldata extraArgs
    79	  ) external payable returns (uint256 requestId);
    80	
    81	  function link() external view returns (address);
    82	  function linkNativeFeed() external view returns (address);
    83	}

     7	  bytes4 public constant EXTRA_ARGS_V1_TAG = bytes4(keccak256("VRF ExtraArgsV1"));

     9	  struct ExtraArgsV1 {
    10	    bool nativePayment;
    11	  }

     4	import {LinkTokenInterface} from "../../shared/interfaces/LinkTokenInterface.sol";
     5	import {IVRFV2PlusWrapper} from "./interfaces/IVRFV2PlusWrapper.sol";
     6	
     7	/**
     8	 *
     9	 * @notice Interface for contracts using VRF randomness through the VRF V2 wrapper
    10	 * ********************************************************************************
    11	 * @dev PURPOSE
    12	 *
    13	 * @dev Create VRF V2+ requests without the need for subscription management. Rather than creating
    14	 * @dev and funding a VRF V2+ subscription, a user can use this wrapper to create one off requests,
    15	 * @dev paying up front rather than at fulfillment.
    16	 *
    17	 * @dev Since the price is determined using the gas price of the request transaction rather than
    18	 * @dev the fulfillment transaction, the wrapper charges an additional premium on callback gas
    19	 * @dev usage, in addition to some extra overhead costs associated with the VRFV2Wrapper contract.
    20	 * *****************************************************************************
    21	 * @dev USAGE
    22	 *
    23	 * @dev Calling contracts must inherit from VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase. The consumer must be funded
    24	 * @dev with enough LINK or ether to make the request, otherwise requests will revert. To request randomness,
    25	 * @dev call the 'requestRandomWords' function with the desired VRF parameters. This function handles
    26	 * @dev paying for the request based on the current pricing.
    27	 *
    28	 * @dev Consumers must implement the fullfillRandomWords function, which will be called during
    29	 * @dev fulfillment with the randomness result.
    30	 */
    31	abstract contract VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase {
    32	  error OnlyVRFWrapperCanFulfill(address have, address want);
    33	
    34	  LinkTokenInterface internal immutable i_linkToken;
    35	  IVRFV2PlusWrapper public immutable i_vrfV2PlusWrapper;
    36	
    37	  /**
    38	   * @param _vrfV2PlusWrapper is the address of the VRFV2Wrapper contract
    39	   */
    40	  constructor(
    41	    address _vrfV2PlusWrapper
    42	  ) {
    43	    IVRFV2PlusWrapper vrfV2PlusWrapper = IVRFV2PlusWrapper(_vrfV2PlusWrapper);
    44	
    45	    i_linkToken = LinkTokenInterface(vrfV2PlusWrapper.link());
    46	    i_vrfV2PlusWrapper = vrfV2PlusWrapper;
    47	  }
    48	
    49	  /**
    50	   * @dev Requests randomness from the VRF V2+ wrapper.
    51	   *
    52	   * @param _callbackGasLimit is the gas limit that should be used when calling the consumer's
    53	   *        fulfillRandomWords function.
    54	   * @param _requestConfirmations is the number of confirmations to wait before fulfilling the
    55	   *        request. A higher number of confirmations increases security by reducing the likelihood
    56	   *        that a chain re-org changes a published randomness outcome.
    57	   * @param _numWords is the number of random words to request.
    58	   *
    59	   * @return requestId is the VRF V2+ request ID of the newly created randomness request.
    60	   */
    61	  // solhint-disable-next-line chainlink-solidity/prefix-internal-functions-with-underscore
    62	  function requestRandomness(
    63	    uint32 _callbackGasLimit,
    64	    uint16 _requestConfirmations,
    65	    uint32 _numWords,
    66	    bytes memory extraArgs
    67	  ) internal returns (uint256 requestId, uint256 reqPrice) {
    68	    reqPrice = i_vrfV2PlusWrapper.calculateRequestPrice(_callbackGasLimit, _numWords);
    69	    i_linkToken.transferAndCall(
    70	      address(i_vrfV2PlusWrapper), reqPrice, abi.encode(_callbackGasLimit, _requestConfirmations, _numWords, extraArgs)
    71	    );
    72	    return (i_vrfV2PlusWrapper.lastRequestId(), reqPrice);
    73	  }
    74	
    75	  // solhint-disable-next-line chainlink-solidity/prefix-internal-functions-with-underscore
    76	  function requestRandomnessPayInNative(
    77	    uint32 _callbackGasLimit,
    78	    uint16 _requestConfirmations,
    79	    uint32 _numWords,
    80	    bytes memory extraArgs
    81	  ) internal returns (uint256 requestId, uint256 requestPrice) {
    82	    requestPrice = i_vrfV2PlusWrapper.calculateRequestPriceNative(_callbackGasLimit, _numWords);
    83	    return (
    84	      i_vrfV2PlusWrapper.requestRandomWordsInNative{value: requestPrice}(
    85	        _callbackGasLimit, _requestConfirmations, _numWords, extraArgs
    86	      ),
    87	      requestPrice
    88	    );
    89	  }
    90	
    91	  /**
    92	   * @notice fulfillRandomWords handles the VRF V2 wrapper response. The consuming contract must
    93	   * @notice implement it.
    94	   *
    95	   * @param _requestId is the VRF V2 request ID.
    96	   * @param _randomWords is the randomness result.
    97	   */
    98	  // solhint-disable-next-line chainlink-solidity/prefix-internal-functions-with-underscore
    99	  function fulfillRandomWords(uint256 _requestId, uint256[] memory _randomWords) internal virtual;
   100	
   101	  function rawFulfillRandomWords(uint256 _requestId, uint256[] memory _randomWords) external {
   102	    address vrfWrapperAddr = address(i_vrfV2PlusWrapper);
   103	    if (msg.sender != vrfWrapperAddr) {
   104	      revert OnlyVRFWrapperCanFulfill(msg.sender, vrfWrapperAddr);
   105	    }
   106	    fulfillRandomWords(_requestId, _randomWords);
   107	  }
   108	
   109	  /// @notice getBalance returns the native balance of the consumer contract
   110	  function getBalance() public view returns (uint256) {
   111	    return address(this).balance;
   112	  }
   113	
   114	  /// @notice getLinkToken returns the link token contract
   115	  function getLinkToken() public view returns (LinkTokenInterface) {
   116	    return i_linkToken;
   117	  }
   118	}

     3	
     4	interface IVRFV2PlusWrapper {
     5	  /**
     6	   * @return the request ID of the most recent VRF V2 request made by this wrapper. This should only
     7	   * be relied option within the same transaction that the request was made.
     8	   */
     9	  function lastRequestId() external view returns (uint256);
    10	
    11	  /**
    12	   * @notice Calculates the price of a VRF request with the given callbackGasLimit at the current
    13	   * @notice block.
    14	   *
    15	   * @dev This function relies on the transaction gas price which is not automatically set during
    16	   * @dev simulation. To estimate the price at a specific gas price, use the estimatePrice function.
    17	   *
    18	   * @param _callbackGasLimit is the gas limit used to estimate the price.
    19	   * @param _numWords is the number of words to request.
    20	   */
    21	  function calculateRequestPrice(uint32 _callbackGasLimit, uint32 _numWords) external view returns (uint256);
    22	
    23	  /**
    24	   * @notice Calculates the price of a VRF request in native with the given callbackGasLimit at the current
    25	   * @notice block.
    26	   *
    27	   * @dev This function relies on the transaction gas price which is not automatically set during
    28	   * @dev simulation. To estimate the price at a specific gas price, use the estimatePrice function.
    29	   *
    30	   * @param _callbackGasLimit is the gas limit used to estimate the price.
    31	   * @param _numWords is the number of words to request.
    32	   */
    33	  function calculateRequestPriceNative(uint32 _callbackGasLimit, uint32 _numWords) external view returns (uint256);
    34	
    35	  /**
    36	   * @notice Estimates the price of a VRF request with a specific gas limit and gas price.
    37	   *
    38	   * @dev This is a convenience function that can be called in simulation to better understand
    39	   * @dev pricing.
    40	   *
    41	   * @param _callbackGasLimit is the gas limit used to estimate the price.
    42	   * @param _numWords is the number of words to request.
    43	   * @param _requestGasPriceWei is the gas price in wei used for the estimation.
    44	   */
    45	  function estimateRequestPrice(
    46	    uint32 _callbackGasLimit,
    47	    uint32 _numWords,
    48	    uint256 _requestGasPriceWei
    49	  ) external view returns (uint256);
    50	
    51	  /**
    52	   * @notice Estimates the price of a VRF request in native with a specific gas limit and gas price.
    53	   *
    54	   * @dev This is a convenience function that can be called in simulation to better understand
    55	   * @dev pricing.
    56	   *
    57	   * @param _callbackGasLimit is the gas limit used to estimate the price.
    58	   * @param _numWords is the number of words to request.
    59	   * @param _requestGasPriceWei is the gas price in wei used for the estimation.
    60	   */
    61	  function estimateRequestPriceNative(
    62	    uint32 _callbackGasLimit,
    63	    uint32 _numWords,
    64	    uint256 _requestGasPriceWei
    65	  ) external view returns (uint256);
    66	
    67	  /**
    68	   * @notice Requests randomness from the VRF V2 wrapper, paying in native token.
    69	   *
    70	   * @param _callbackGasLimit is the gas limit for the request.
    71	   * @param _requestConfirmations number of request confirmations to wait before serving a request.
    72	   * @param _numWords is the number of words to request.
    73	   */
    74	  function requestRandomWordsInNative(
    75	    uint32 _callbackGasLimit,
    76	    uint16 _requestConfirmations,
    77	    uint32 _numWords,
    78	    bytes calldata extraArgs
    79	  ) external payable returns (uint256 requestId);
    80	
    81	  function link() external view returns (address);
    82	  function linkNativeFeed() external view returns (address);
    83	}
